window-layout.text: The DENIS main window is a single shell hosting four top-level tabs plus a menu bar. It opens maximized on the Estimate tab.

The window title starts as DENIS v1.0.0. After a Save, Save As..., or Load All... it gains the file name, e.g. DENIS v1.0.0 - my_run.yaml, so you can always see which configuration is in play. The icon is the bundled denis.ico, falling back to a generic atom glyph if that file is missing.

A rolodex-style tab bar runs across the top; the active tab fuses into the pane below with an accent underline (navy folder-tabs under the Classic 98 theme), and inactive tabs sit slightly lower and darker. Each tab carries a Lucide icon and is added in this fixed order:

rows: Predict beam time and simulate HFS spectra before a measurement
Load ASDF runs, gate, bin, and overlay a trial HFS model
Browse reports, re-render plots, export, compute isotope shifts

window-layout.text: Click any tab to switch. The window remembers nothing about which tab was active across launches; it always starts on Estimate. For a guided tour of what each tab does, see [[four-tab-tour]].

window-layout.caption: The DENIS main window on launch: the four-tab rolodex bar (Estimate, Pre-Analysis, Analysis, Results) with the File/Edit/View/Run/Tools/Help menu bar above it and the status bar at the bottom.

menu-bar.text: Six menus run across the top of the window. Every entry carries a Lucide icon. This page maps them; the deeper behaviors each have their own page.

rows: Save, Save As..., Load All..., Save Tab As..., Load Tab..., New Window, Settings..., Exit
Zoom In, Zoom Out, Reset Zoom, and a disabled Zoom: NN% label
Schmidt Moment Calculator, Shell Configuration Plotter, Unit Converter, SHG Crystal Angle Calculator, SFG / DFG Calculator, Quick Plot, NIST ASD Browser…
Save (writes to the current file; falls back to Save As when none is loaded)
Save As... (every tab to a chosen YAML)

menu-bar.text: Plain Ctrl+S is a true editor-style Save: once a file is loaded it writes with no dialog. Save Tab As... has no shortcut and always shows a dialog. See [[save-all-vs-tab]] for the full semantics.

Edit > Split File… opens the virtual-split editor (pick an ASDF, place a voltage cut, and write .vasdf sidecars) — covered in [[split-file-editor]]. The Tools menu calculators each have their own page under [[tools]].

menu-bar.caption: The File menu expanded, showing Save All / Load All / Save Tab / Load Tab / Settings / Exit with their icons.

save-load-config.text: DENIS stores all working state in a single YAML file. The File menu follows the standard editor model: Save writes to the current file with no dialog, Save As... picks a new file, and Save Tab As... writes a single tab.
Save, Save As, and Save Tab As

items: Save (Ctrl+S) writes to the currently loaded file with no dialog; when none is loaded it falls through to Save As.

Save As... (Ctrl+Shift+S) writes the top-level sections — estimate, preanalysis, and analysis — to one .yaml, plus the shared registries when present: scan_filters, calibrations, calibration_acks, and nist_asd.
Save Tab As... writes only the active tab's section, merging into an existing file (other sections on disk are preserved). It also refreshes the shared registries.
If you omit the extension, .yaml is appended automatically.

save-load-config.text: Load All restores every recognized section present in the file and reports which tabs were loaded. Load Tab loads only the current tab's section; if that section is absent, DENIS tells you which sections the file actually contains. A legacy estimate config (top-level element/Z/isotopes keys, no estimate: wrapper) is detected and loaded into the Estimate tab.
The Results tab has no YAML section. Save Tab / Load Tab on Results reports "This tab does not support saving/loading."
Remembered directories and the close prompt

Save and Load remember separate last-used directories, so loading from one folder and saving to another never clobber each other; both fall back to ./configs/ when the remembered path no longer exists. DENIS fingerprints the full save state: closing an untouched or freshly-saved session never prompts, while a dirty one offers Save (to the current file, or Save As when none is loaded), Don't Save, and Cancel (Cancel is the default). See [[exit-prompt]].
If a loaded file references data files that are no longer on disk, the missing-file relocation flow runs first — see [[missing-file-relocation]]. For the exact key layout, see [[save-yaml-format]].

save-load-config.code:
estimate:
  element: Co
  ...
  last_run: {...}   # restores plots/log on load
preanalysis:
  ...
analysis:
  projects: [...]
scan_filters:      # optional shared registries
calibrations:
calibration_acks:
nist_asd:

save-load-config.caption: The Missing Files dialog listing unfound data files with Locate Files... / Skip Missing / Cancel buttons.

undo-redo.text: A single application-wide undo stack backs Edit > Undo (Ctrl+Z) and Edit > Redo (Ctrl+Y). It holds up to 200 steps.

An application-level event filter watches every numeric spinbox. When a spinbox gains focus it snapshots the current value; when it loses focus (or right before you press Ctrl+Z) it pushes an undo command if the value changed. Because tracking is keyed on focus, spinboxes that are created on the fly — a newly added isotope, a new analysis block — are picked up automatically the first time you click into them, with no rescan.

Undoing or redoing doesn't just flip a number quietly. DENIS surfaces the affected widget: it switches to the owning top-level tab and sub-tab, scrolls the widget into view inside its scroll area, then pulses an amber highlight on it so you see exactly what moved. (The very first redo right after an edit skips the reveal, since you are already looking at the field.)

Undo is spinbox-centric. Numeric-field edits are tracked generically; text fields, combo boxes, and structural changes (adding/removing files or projects) are not captured by this generic mechanism unless a feature opts in explicitly. Treat Undo as "undo a numeric edit," not "undo everything."
The [[plot-editor|Plot Editor]] keeps its own Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y history for plot edits while it is open — separate from this application-wide spinbox stack.
Press Ctrl+Z immediately after typing into a spinbox and it still works: any in-flight edit is committed before the undo runs.

undo-redo.caption: An undo in progress: DENIS has switched to the affected tab and flashed an amber highlight on the spinbox whose value was reverted.

clipboard-shortcuts.text: Plain Qt spinboxes only copy/paste text you have manually selected inside them. DENIS adds application-wide Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V handling so numeric fields behave the way you expect.

items: Ctrl+C with nothing selected copies the spinbox's whole displayed value. If you have highlighted part of the text, the normal copy of just that selection runs instead.

Ctrl+V parses the clipboard as a number and sets the field. Integer spinboxes round to the nearest whole number; if the clipboard isn't a valid number the paste is silently swallowed (no crash, no change).

clipboard-shortcuts.text: Fields backed by ScientificSpinBox accept and display scientific notation (e.g. 1.5e-3). They format compactly with %.6g, so values stay readable across many orders of magnitude, and they parse partial input like 1e while you type. All numeric fields use a US-English locale, forcing a dot as the decimal separator regardless of your system locale.
Pasting into a numeric field is also undoable — the value change is captured by the same event filter described in [[undo-redo]].

zoom.text: View > Zoom changes the application font point size — a quick way to make text bigger or smaller without restarting. It is not a true pixel scale.

rows: Increase font by one point (up to +10)
Decrease font by one point (down to -5)
Return to the base font size

zoom.text: The level is clamped to the range -5..+10 and persisted as zoom_level, so it survives restarts; the resulting font never drops below 6pt. Beyond the global font, zoom rescales the fixed-width Analysis blocks and the Estimate global-parameters panel so layouts stay proportional. The current percentage shows as a disabled Zoom: NN% label in the View menu and flashes briefly in the [[status-bar]].

Zoom is distinct from the UI scale setting in [[general-settings]]. UI scale sets QT_SCALE_FACTOR before the application starts (a true DPI scale) and therefore requires a restart; zoom is live and only changes font size.

run-open-output.text: The Run menu has a single action, Open Output Folder, which opens DENIS's root output directory in your operating-system file browser.
The root comes from the output_directory preference in [[output-settings]] — not from the per-run output field on the Estimate tab. Inside that root, results are organized into two subfolders:

items: <root>/estimates — written by the Estimate tab.
<root>/analysis — written by the Analysis tab (project iterations and artifacts).

run-open-output.text: The folder is auto-created the moment you trigger the action, so a first-time user who hasn't run anything yet won't hit a "directory does not exist" error. DENIS uses explorer on Windows, open on macOS, and xdg-open on Linux.

plot-editor.text: The Plot Editor is a reusable, modeless dialog that edits the live matplotlib figure in real time and leaves the dialog open while you keep working. Open it by right-clicking any plot canvas in DENIS and choosing Edit plot… (suppressed while a toolbar pan/zoom tool is engaged), or with the Edit Plot buttons in Estimate, Pre-Analysis, Analysis, and Results.

rows: Canvas width/height (in/mm/px) and DPI; subplot margins; an Auto (Tight Layout) button
Per-axes title and X/Y labels with positions, a real font-family picker with live preview, sizes, limits, major/minor ticks, linear/log scale, tick direction, and grid

Per-artist color, width, style, marker, alpha, visibility, position, rotation, and z-order; for text/annotations a font-size spin (4–72 pt), font family, Bold/Italic, and the arrow-tip position; a Remove artist button

New Text, Annotation (text + arrow), vertical/horizontal lines and spans — placed by numeric coordinates or by clicking the plot (annotations and spans take two clicks); added artists are fully editable and removable
Position, font size, frame visibility and alpha, columns, and title (Apply Legend)
Export DPI (default 300); Overwrite Original; Save as PNG / PDF / SVG

plot-editor.text: When the source figure has siblings (the Pre-Analysis spectrum with its TOF and Timestamp figures), a Plot: selector at the top switches between them.

Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y (and Ctrl+Shift+Z) step through snapshots of the figure taken after every change — including removing an artist you just added. The history resets when you switch to a different figure in the Plot: selector.

The Artists tab has a Click to select / drag on plot checkbox. With it on, clicking a line, scatter, or error-bar on the plot selects it in the Artists list, and you can click-and-drag any text label or annotation arrow to reposition it. For an annotation arrow the label and the arrow tip move together so the arrow stays attached.

Remove artist truly deletes elements you added in the Add tab. Renderer-owned artists with an id tag (the isotope-shift δν arrows and labels) stay removed across re-renders; untagged renderer artists are hidden instead (same as unticking Visible).

items: Overwrite Original writes back over the source image file — it is enabled only when DENIS knows the source path (Results plots).
Save as PNG / PDF / SVG exports a fresh copy at the chosen Export DPI.

For Results plots backed by an .npz file, edits also persist to a .style.json sidecar so they survive a re-render — see [[res-style-json]]. On other surfaces the edits live only until the plot is redrawn; use the Export tab to keep them.

status-bar.text: The bottom status bar, managed by StatusBarManager, reports timestamped events, fitting progress, and an attention flash. It starts at Ready.

items: Timestamped messages (e.g. save/load confirmations, zoom percentage) are prefixed with [HH:MM:SS] and auto-clear back to Ready after 8 seconds.
Persistent messages stay until something replaces them — used for ongoing operations like "Estimation running...".
An embedded progress bar (max width 200px) appears during fits, fed by the Analysis fit-progress signal, and auto-hides about 3 seconds after reaching 100%.

status-bar.text: When an analysis run finishes while you are on another tab, the status bar pulses an amber background and nudges you with a "click the Results tab to view" message. DENIS deliberately does not steal focus by switching tabs for you. The flash keeps pulsing until you open the [[tab-results|Results]] tab, at which point it stops and the bar returns to Ready.

status-bar.caption: Status bar states stacked: a normal timestamped message, the embedded fitting progress bar, and the amber 'analysis complete - click the Results tab' flash.

help-about.text: Help > About opens a small dialog with the DENIS logo and the project's identity and credits.

items: The DENIS logo and version, DENIS v1.0.0.
The name expansion: Doppler Estimation and Numerical Inference for Spectroscopy.
A one-line scope summary: estimation, pre-analysis, fitting, and results.
Hyperlinked credits: satlas2 (fitting and spectrum estimation) and cls_tools (IGISOL-style ASDF file reading).
Developer contact: Arda Kayaalp, arda.kayaalp@kuleuven.be, and a note that the GUI is built with PySide6 + matplotlib.

help-about.text: The window title and the About box both say DENIS. "CLS Toolkit" appears only as the internal module description in the source and is not a user-facing product name.
The same Help menu also has Documentation (F1), which opens this interactive manual.

help-about.caption: The About DENIS dialog showing the logo, version, the D-E-N-I-S name expansion, the satlas2 and cls_tools links, and developer contact.

est-layout.text: The Estimate tab predicts collinear-laser-spectroscopy measurement times and simulates hyperfine (HFS) spectra. Since the 2026-07 UI overhaul it is a single surface (no sub-tabs): three resizable columns — element/transition parameters, the isotope list, and a right column stacking Run Options, the plot display, and the log. The ⛶ button on the plot panel expands the plots over the whole tab.

items: Column 1 - global parameters: Element && Transition, Beam, Laser, Linewidth, Scan, Statistics (Timing Mode), and Advanced groups in a scroll area. Its width band is measured from the content at runtime (so labels never clip at any font/DPI). See [[est-global-params-groups]].
Column 2 - isotope list: a dynamic, scrollable list of isotope panels added with + Add Isotope, color-striped by position. See [[est-isotope-list]].

Column 3 - Run Options, plots && log: the Run Options group (output directory, palette, Generate plots, and the Run Estimation / Load Estimation... buttons) sits at its natural height; below it a vertical splitter holds the plot panel over the log. See [[est-run-options]] and [[est-plots-subtab]].

est-layout.text: Only column 3 stretches when you widen the window; columns 1 and 2 keep their bands. Zooming re-measures column 1 instead of scaling stale constants.
A small Info button at the bottom of the tab opens a scrollable HTML help dialog summarising every group on the tab.

est-layout.caption: The Estimate tab's single surface: global parameters, the isotope list, and the Run Options / plots / log column, with splitter handles between them.

est-element-transition.text: The Element && Transition group (column 1) identifies the atom and the atomic transition you intend to measure. It feeds the rest-frame transition frequency and the per-isotope atomic-mass lookup.

rows: Chemical symbol (e.g. Co, Ge). Typing a known symbol sets Z automatically.
Atomic number (proton number), range 1-118. Changing Z fills in the matching symbol.
Lower energy level of the transition (0-200000 cm⁻¹).
Upper energy level of the transition (0-200000 cm⁻¹).
Total angular momentum J of the lower level (half-integer allowed, step 0.5).
Total angular momentum J of the upper level (half-integer allowed, step 0.5).

est-element-transition.text: Element and Z are kept in sync in both directions. Typing a recognised symbol writes Z; editing Z writes the symbol. Z also propagates to every isotope panel so each one can show its atomic mass in amu (looked up from the bundled IUPAC/AME table for the current Z and mass number A) - see [[est-isotope-nuclear]].
DENIS computes the rest-frame transition frequency from the two energy levels. The level difference in cm⁻¹ is converted to Hz via the speed of light (CM_TO_HZ = c × 100) and reported in MHz:

est-element-transition.name: transition-frequency
est-element-transition.caption: Rest-frame transition frequency from the lower and upper levels.

est-laser.text: The Laser group (column 1) sets the harmonic multiplier and chooses how DENIS knows the laser frequency: you give it directly (Setpoint) or have DENIS back-solve it from an isotope's resonance (Anchor to isotope).
Harmonic is the laser harmonic multiplier (1-10; 1 = fundamental, 2 = SHG, 4 = FHG). The effective probing wavenumber is the fundamental setpoint multiplied by this harmonic.
Two radio buttons select the mode. Picking one disables the other's fields:

rows: Use the fundamental laser wavenumber directly.
DENIS back-solves the laser frequency so the named isotope's centroid sits at V0 − dV, and logs the derived setpoint.

est-laser.text: In Anchor to isotope mode DENIS computes the resonance voltage V_res = V0 − dV, inverts the Doppler relation to get the laser frequency, then converts it back to a fundamental wavenumber and records it as the derived setpoint in the run log.

est-laser.name: laser-frequency-resonance
est-laser.caption: Laser frequency that places a chosen centroid on resonance (geometry-dependent).

est-laser.name: resonance-beta
est-laser.caption: Beam beta implied by the laser/rest frequency ratio in each geometry.

est-laser.text: The two modes are exclusive in both the GUI and the config parser. A saved config that specifies both setpoint_cm and anchor, or neither, is rejected at load with an error.

est-laser.caption: The Laser group with Harmonic, the Setpoint radio (with its wavenumber field), and the Anchor-to-isotope radio (with isotope label, dV, and gs/isomer state). Capture in anchor mode so the setpoint field is greyed out.

est-linewidth-scan.text: The Linewidth and Scan groups (column 1) set the spectral width used for simulated spectra and the voltage-scan geometry used for timing.

FWHM (MHz) is a single full-width-at-half-maximum (default 100, minimum 0.1) covering Doppler plus laser broadening. It is the Gaussian width of every simulated peak; it does not affect timing. Internally it is converted to a Gaussian sigma:

rows: Total scan window, centred on the beam voltage V0.
Voltage per DAC step (timing mode only).
Integration time per step (timing mode only).

est-linewidth-scan.text: Step size and Dwell time are disabled and omitted from the saved config in spectrum-only mode (when the Statistics group is unchecked). Only Voltage range is always written. See [[est-statistics]].
The simulated intensity is a sum of Gaussians, one per HFS peak, evaluated against the Doppler-shifted frequency seen across the voltage window:

est-linewidth-scan.name: simulated-spectrum
est-linewidth-scan.caption: Simulated HFS spectrum as a sum of Gaussians over the scan window.

est-statistics.text: The Statistics (Timing Mode) group is a checkable group box that acts as the master switch for timing on this tab.
When checked (the default), DENIS computes measurement-time estimates and the group exposes two controls:

rows: Statistical significance target (number of sigma; minimum 0.1).
Measure all peaks for the same time, based on the strongest peak assuming full yield.

est-statistics.text: The default required significance is 3.0 sigma, not 5. The Uniform timing checkbox here is the global default; any isotope can override it locally - see [[est-isotope-rates]].

Unchecking the group puts the whole tab in spectrum-only mode: timing math is skipped, and every isotope's Rates && Timing and Background groups (and yield controls) are hidden. The Scan group's step size and dwell time are also disabled. The config parser infers spectrum_only from the absence of a statistics block, so spectrum-only configs simply omit it.
In timing mode the on-peak integration time for a peak with signal rate S and background B follows from the required significance:

est-statistics.name: on-peak-time
est-statistics.caption: On-peak integration time for a target significance.

est-statistics.code:
# Real estimate defaults
required_sigma = 3.0     # Statistics group
voltage_kV     = 30.0    # Beam
dwell_time_ms  = 200     # Scan
fwhm_MHz       = 100     # Linewidth
efficiency     = 0.001   # per-isotope Rates
est-statistics.caption: Out-of-the-box defaults across the estimate groups.

est-advanced-gs.text: The Advanced group (column 1) holds a single control: the Schmidt g_s factor, a spin-g-factor quenching factor applied by every Schmidt-moment calculation on this tab.

rows: Quenching of the free-nucleon spin g-factor. 1.0 = free nucleon; typical quenched values are 0.6-0.8.

est-advanced-gs.text: The factor feeds the single-particle and two-particle Schmidt formulas used when an isotope or isomer derives its magnetic moment from the shell model - see [[est-schmidt-widget]].

est-advanced-gs.name: schmidt-proton
est-advanced-gs.caption: Single-particle Schmidt moment for a proton (g_s enters the spin term).

est-advanced-gs.name: schmidt-neutron
est-advanced-gs.caption: Single-particle Schmidt moment for a neutron.

est-advanced-gs.text: The factor is written to the config only when it differs from 1.0; a default value is simply omitted. Note the auto-fill that populates the μ field as you build a Schmidt spec always uses g_s = 1 (the unquenched value); the configured g_s factor is applied later in the run.

est-isotope-list.text: Column 2 holds a dynamic list of isotope panels. Each panel configures one isotope's nuclear data, rates, background, and optional isomer.

items: Click + Add Isotope to append a new panel; a live label next to it reads N isotopes.
Each panel has a Remove button in its header.
Panels are titled Isotope 1, Isotope 2, ... and renumber automatically when you remove or reorder them.

est-isotope-list.text: Each panel has a drag handle (the ☰ grip) in its header. Press and drag it to move the panel; dropping it over another panel reorders the list and renumbers every panel.

Exactly one panel can be the Reference (its A and B hyperfine constants scale the others). Ticking Reference on a new panel clears it on the previous one. The reference panel is drawn with a blue border, and its Override A/B constants tick is forced on and locked so you must supply explicit measured constants for it.
When a saved config is loaded, the reference is matched to a panel by mass number A (via set_reference_from_config), and that panel's A/B constants are populated from the saved reference block.

est-isotope-list.caption: Column 2 with the '+ Add Isotope' button and isotope count, plus two isotope panels - one marked Reference with a blue border and its drag handle visible.

est-isotope-nuclear.text: Every isotope panel's top form holds its nuclear parameters. These define the hyperfine structure and the centroid position relative to the reference.

rows: Mass number (1-300). A live label beside it shows the atomic mass in amu for the current Z and A, looked up from the IUPAC/AME table (or (not in table)).
Display label, e.g. 59Co. Must match the anchor label if used in [[est-laser]].
Nuclear spin (half-integer allowed; 0 for even-even nuclei).
Magnetic moment in nuclear magnetons. Leave 0 if deriving it from Schmidt.
Electric quadrupole moment in barns (0 for I = 0 or I = 1/2).
This isotope's centroid minus the reference centroid.

est-isotope-nuclear.text: The Isotope shift (MHz) is defined as (this isotope's centroid − reference centroid). A positive value means this isotope sits at higher frequency than the reference. Leave it at 0 for the reference itself.

The amu label updates live as you change A or the global Z. If μ is left at 0 while a Schmidt spec is active, DENIS auto-fills μ with the unquenched Schmidt value so downstream A-scaling never divides by zero - see [[est-schmidt-widget]].

est-isotope-nuclear.caption: An isotope panel expanded to show the nuclear fields (A with amu label, Label, I, mu, Q, isotope shift) and, below, the isomer and Schmidt sub-panels.

est-isotope-rates.text: The Rates && Timing group on each isotope panel supplies the numbers that drive the timing estimate. It is shown only in timing mode and hidden entirely in spectrum-only mode.

rows: Ion production rate at the interaction region (a scientific-notation spinbox).
Fraction of ions producing detected photons (0-1; 0.001 = 1 per 1000).
Number of strongest HFS peaks to include in the timing estimate (1-100).
When ticked, enables the per-isotope Uniform timing combo below it.
Off / On - this isotope's override of the global uniform-timing setting.

est-isotope-rates.text: The GUI label is Yield (ions/s), not cps. The per-isotope Uniform timing override wins over the global default at run time, and is written to the config only when Override uniform timing is ticked.
The per-peak signal rate combines yield, efficiency, and the peak's relative intensity:

est-isotope-rates.name: signal-rate
est-isotope-rates.caption: Detected signal rate for a single HFS peak.

est-isotope-background.text: The Background group on each isotope panel selects the background model used in the timing estimate. It is shown only in timing mode.
In TOF-gated mode the effective background collapses to the continuous rate scaled by the ratio of the gate width to the dwell time:

est-isotope-background.name: tof-gated-background
est-isotope-background.caption: Effective background rate after time-of-flight gating.
How the parser folds the gate width and dwell into one effective rate.

est-isotope-background.text: In timing mode an isotope with no background specified raises a validation error at load. Unit wording differs between surfaces: the control tooltip says counts/s per voltage step (Hz), while the Info HTML calls it counts/bin - treat the field as a count rate in Hz, which is how the parser uses it.

est-isotope-ab-override.text: By default a non-reference isotope's hyperfine A and B constants are scaled from the reference using nuclear-moment ratios. The Override A/B constants tick lets you supply explicit measured constants instead.
The magnetic-dipole constant A scales with the ratio of magnetic moments and spins; the electric-quadrupole constant B scales with the ratio of quadrupole moments:

est-isotope-ab-override.name: a-scaling
est-isotope-ab-override.caption: A constant scaled from the reference.

est-isotope-ab-override.name: b-scaling
est-isotope-ab-override.caption: B constant scaled from the reference.

est-isotope-ab-override.text: Ticking Override A/B constants reveals four fields - A_lower, B_lower, A_upper, B_upper (all in MHz) - for the lower and upper levels of the transition. Use these when you have measured constants and do not want them inferred.
The reference isotope always has this override forced on and locked: it must carry explicit A/B constants because every other isotope scales from it. See [[est-isotope-list]].

est-schmidt-widget.text: A collapsible Schmidt widget on each isotope (and isomer) panel lets you derive the magnetic moment μ from the nuclear shell model instead of typing it.
Tick Use Schmidt moment to reveal the configuration body. Choose Single particle or Two particles:

rows: Type (proton / neutron) and Orbital (from the shell-model orbital list, e.g. 1f7/2).
Type 1 + Orbital 1, Type 2 + Orbital 2, and a Total I for the coupling.

est-schmidt-widget.text: Whenever you change the spec (or first tick the box), DENIS computes the unquenched Schmidt moment (g_s = 1) and writes it into the panel's μ field. This guarantees the A-scaling step never divides by zero. The fill is recorded on the global undo stack, so Ctrl+Z reverts to the previous μ.

est-schmidt-widget.name: two-particle-lande
est-schmidt-widget.caption: Two-particle weak-coupling Lande g and resulting moment.

est-schmidt-widget.text: The configured quenching factor (g_s, in [[est-advanced-gs]]) is applied later, during the run; the in-form auto-fill always uses the unquenched value. The standalone [[tool-schmidt]] mirrors this widget.

est-isomers.text: Tick Has isomer on an isotope panel to expand an isomer sub-panel. The isomer carries its own nuclear data, peak count, and yield, and can have its own A/B override and Schmidt widget.
The sub-panel repeats I, μ, Q, Isotope shift (MHz), and Peaks to measure, plus a Plot with ground state checkbox (on by default) that overlays the isomer on the ground-state spectrum.
In timing mode the isomer needs exactly one yield method, chosen by radio:

rows: Fraction of total yield going to the ground state; the isomer gets the remainder.
Absolute isomer yield, independent of the ground state.
Auto-split the g.s./isomer ratio from spin-distribution statistics.

est-isomers.text: The spin-distribution split weights states by their (2J+1) multiplicity and a Gaussian in J:

est-isomers.name: spin-distribution-ratio
est-isomers.caption: Ground-state to isomer population ratio from a spin distribution.

est-isomers.text: In timing mode the config parser requires exactly one yield method per isomer - specifying none, or more than one, is a load error. In spectrum-only mode the yield method is omitted.

est-run-options.text: Column 3 (the Run Options group plus the log) is where you point the output, pick a palette, kick off the run, and watch progress stream in.

rows: Where results are written; defaults to <output_root>/estimates. Use Browse... to change it.
When ticked (default), HFS spectra and overview PDFs are produced alongside the YAML.

est-run-options.text: Run Estimation and Load Estimation... sit on one row inside the Run Options group. Run starts the calculation: a read-only, monospaced, syntax-highlighted log at the bottom of the column streams progress and results; Clear empties it. The log is also saved to a .log file in the run's cls_<timestamp> output folder, next to the YAML config, the plot data (estimate_results.npz) and the peak table (peaks.csv).
What the log contains, in order

items: A header and the (possibly anchor-derived) laser setpoint.
Per-isotope timing tables with subtotals, and per-isomer tables.
A Nuclear parameters && HFS constants summary table.
The GRAND TOTAL measurement time (hours and 8-hour shifts).
Two peak lists: Peak List (sorted by intensity) and Peak List (sorted by voltage).

est-run-options.text: Load Estimation... reopens any previous run folder for viewing — plots, peak table, and log restore without re-running and without creating new output. The save file also records the last run, so a saved session restores it automatically on load. Picking a folder that is not a run folder shows a hint instead of failing.

est-run-options.caption: Column 3 showing the Run Options group (output directory + Browse, color palette, Generate plots), the bold Run Estimation button, and the syntax-highlighted log with a Grand Total and a peak list visible.

est-plots-subtab.text: The plot panel (column 3) renders the simulated spectra natively on an embedded matplotlib canvas with a navigation toolbar. Until a run completes it shows a placeholder reading Run a calculation to see plots here. Its width tracks the column, and the ⛶ toggle expands the plots over the whole tab.

rows: One panel per isotope (and isomer); dashed vertical lines mark the measured peaks.
All isotopes overlaid on one spectrum.
A sortable table: Isotope, State, Shift (MHz), Offset (MHz), dV (V), V_acc (V), Intensity.

items: The matplotlib navigation toolbar gives pan, zoom, and save on the canvas.
Edit Plot opens the shared plot editor - see [[plot-editor]]. Right-clicking the canvas offers the same Edit plot… entry.
Open PDF opens the exported PDF for the current view. Both buttons are disabled until a run has produced output.

est-plots-subtab.text: Estimation runs from before the .npz persistence existed hold only PDFs. When such a run is loaded via [[est-run-options|Load Estimation...]], its PDF pages are rasterized onto the canvas as stacked images, so pan/zoom/save still work.

est-plots-subtab.caption: The plot panel with the View drop-down set to Individual Spectra, dashed lines marking measured peaks, and the Edit Plot / Open PDF buttons.

est-global-params-groups.text: Every control on this tab serialises to and from a YAML config through to_dict / from_dict methods that mirror the dataclasses in the config parser. This is the format used by Save/Load and by the temporary-config run path.
Where the field names come from

items: GlobalParamsWidget.to_dict/from_dict handles column 1: element, Z, transition, beam, laser, linewidth, scan, optional statistics, optional g_s_factor. The tab-level dict adds last_run — a pointer to the latest run folder so plots, peak table, and log restore on load.
IsotopePanel.to_dict/from_dict (and the nested isomer) handles each isotope's nuclear data, rates, background, A/B override, Schmidt spec, and isomer block.
The config-parser dataclasses define the canonical schema and validate it at load.

est-global-params-groups.text: Some fields are written only under certain conditions, which matters if you hand-edit YAML:

rows: Timing mode; its absence means spectrum-only.
Exactly one of production_ratio / yield_ions_per_sec / spin_distribution_sigma.

est-global-params-groups.text: Validation runs at load: the laser must give exactly one of setpoint/anchor; each timing-mode isotope needs a background; each timing-mode isomer needs exactly one yield method. Violations raise an error rather than loading silently.

pa-overview.text: The Pre-Analysis tab is DENIS's data viewer: it loads collinear-laser-spectroscopy ASDF runs, displays them in a two-pane layout, and lets you gate, bin, and inspect spectra before fitting. Each Pre-Analysis is an independent project sub-tab inside a multi-project container.
A horizontal splitter divides the tab into three resizable columns:

rows: Data Files list (loaded runs), the Plot Options group (x-axis mode, physics parameters, channels, overrides), and the HFS Models panel — trial hyperfine overlays that seed the fitter

pa-overview.text: The left column is fixed-ish (380-540 px) and the center plots take the remaining stretch. Three view controls sit in the corner of the sub-tab row and apply to every open Pre-Analysis project at once: a Layout combo (3 row stacked = ToF / Spectrum / Timestamp rows; 2 row stacked = Spectrum and ToF side by side with the Timestamp strip below — the original Data Viewer arrangement), X / Y grid toggles, and a sun-moon button that switches the plots to dark mode (black canvas, white chrome, neon line colours). All three persist — the dark state both in the global settings (pa_dark_plots) and in the save file.

pa-overview.caption: The full Pre-Analysis tab: left Data Files + Plot Options column, center Spectrum/Calibrations/Cooler Voltage tabs showing the TOF/Spectrum/Timestamp panels, and the right HFS Models column.

pa-overview.text: Pre-Analysis tabs live inside a project container with a + Create Pre-Analysis button at the top. Each project is fully independent (its own files, gates, models, and physics settings). Project sub-tabs are closable, draggable to reorder, and double-clicking a tab renames it. Closing a project prompts for confirmation.
Everything in a project round-trips through the unified YAML save file under the preanalysis section, with one entry per project. See [[pa-save-load]].

pa-loading-files.text: Click Open... in the Data Files header to add one or more runs. The file dialog filters to *.asdf and *.vasdf and remembers the last directory you loaded from.
Each selected path is dispatched by type:

items: Normal ASDF run -- read through clstools into a CLSDataFrame, then cached as per-event numpy arrays (voltage, raw DAC, TOF, channel, timestamp, bunch) plus the calibration tables.
DENIS-labelled merged ASDF -- an export from a previous merge is routed straight to a merged entry (the standard header read would otherwise fail on the merged schema). See [[pa-merging]].
Virtual split (.vasdf) -- a sidecar that loads its parent ASDF and applies a permanent voltage gate so the preview shows only the sub-range. See [[pa-virtual-splits]].

pa-loading-files.text: Paths already in the list are skipped, so re-opening the same file does nothing. Load failures surface as a per-file message box rather than aborting the whole batch.

From the ASDF tree DENIS reads the run number, cooler voltage, laser setpoint, date, atomic mass, and the CalSet/CalReadback calibration arrays. The per-event cooler voltage is reconstructed from the data as:

pa-loading-files.name: cooler-correction
pa-loading-files.caption: Per-event cooler voltage uses Vrfq scaled by VCoolDiv plus VCoolOffset; the calibrated scanning voltage DV_cal is subtracted to give the net beam energy.

pa-loading-files.text: If clstools is not installed the load aborts with a Missing dependency warning -- DENIS reads only IGISOL-style ASDF data through clstools and cannot open any other format.

pa-file-list.text: Every loaded run is one row in the Data Files list. The rows feed both the plots and any Analysis-side import, so checking and styling files here is the single source of truth for what is shown.

rows: Show/hide this run in the plots. Ticked rows are what the spectrum, TOF, and timestamp panels draw.

Opens a popup with Colours (light + dark)… — a dual-mode dialog holding the run's light and dark colours side by side (preset palettes, hex/R,G,B entry, and saved custom slots) — plus an opacity slider and a line style combo.
Re-reads the ASDF from disk — useful for an ongoing scan that is still growing. Hidden on merged entries (their data is in memory).
Gray summary: cooler voltage V=, laser λ= in cm⁻¹, and after loading the run time t=.
A calibration alert — this run's calibration outliers would move its centroid. Click it for the cost in MHz; see [[pa-calibrations]].

pa-file-list.text: Runs are assigned colors in load order from the classic Windows 98 palette (dark halves only — chosen for contrast on the white canvas); in dark mode each run uses its own neon counterpart. Both colours are per-file and editable.

pa-file-list.code:
# light mode (Windows 98 system palette)
DEFAULT_COLORS = ["#000080", "#800000", "#008000", "#800080", "#008080",
                  "#FF0000", "#0000FF", "#808000", "#FF00FF", "#808080"]
# dark mode (index-aligned neon)
NEON_COLORS   = ["#00E5FF", "#FF2D95", "#7CFF3F", "#FFE500", "#FF9A2E",
                  "#22B0FF", "#00FFA3", "#C86BFF", "#FF5C5C", "#F0F0F0"]

items: Check all -- a tri-state master tickbox above the list. It reflects the per-file state (checked / unchecked / mixed square) and clicking it flips every row at once. It is disabled when no files are loaded.
Remove checked -- the button in the header drops every checked row in one click.
Clicking a row highlights it (single selection); the highlighted file feeds the auto-fill buttons in [[pa-plot-options]] and the scan overlay.

pa-file-list.text: Right-clicking a source-file row offers Remove, Check/Uncheck, Set centroid offset... (see [[pa-centroid-offset]]), Filter scans... (see [[pa-scan-filtering]]), Calibration..., and Calibration overview... (see [[pa-calibrations]]). Merged rows instead add View..., Edit..., and Export ASDF... above the common items.
Removing a file via the menu is undoable: Ctrl+Z restores it at its original position. See [[undo-redo]].

pa-spectrum-panels.text: The Spectrum tab shows three panels -- TOF, Spectrum, and Timestamp -- each with its own matplotlib toolbar and draggable dividers. In the default 3 row stacked layout they stack vertically at roughly 3 : 4 : 3; the corner Layout combo switches to 2 row stacked (Spectrum and ToF side by side, Timestamp below). The corner also holds the X/Y grid toggles and the dark-mode button — see [[pa-overview]].

rows: Time-of-flight histogram of the selected events. The header Bin spin sets the bin size (default 1 µs, down to 1 ns for narrow bunches). Used to locate and gate the ion bunch.
The binned counts vs. the chosen x-axis, drawn as a step plot, binned per scan step by default. The header Bin: N × step spin groups N adjacent steps into one bin. This is the main data view.
Event-count histogram over wall-clock time, with a selectable Unit (Seconds / Minutes / Hours / Days) and a Bin size.

pa-spectrum-panels.text: All three histograms are gated by the selected PMT Channels in [[pa-plot-options]] (default 3 & 4). The TOF and timestamp panels always show all events for the selected channels; only the spectrum responds to the TOF and timestamp gates.

items: Scroll-wheel zoom on hover -- roll the wheel over any of the three panels to zoom in/out, centered on the cursor, with no toolbar button needed.
Denser ticks -- each axis gets ~10 major divisions with 5 minor subdivisions so you can read off peak positions for initial guesses.
Each panel's own toolbar gives the standard matplotlib pan/zoom/save controls.

pa-spectrum-panels.text: An Info button at the top of the tab opens a help dialog explaining the panels.

pa-spectrum-panels.caption: The Spectrum tab's three stacked panels (TOF, Spectrum, Timestamp) with their per-panel toolbars and the Timestamp Unit/Bin controls visible.

pa-tof-time-gate.text: Two independent gates filter the spectrum: a TOF gate on the time-of-flight panel and a timestamp gate on the timestamp panel. Each has a Gate tickbox plus a low and a high value box, and each can be drag-set on its panel or typed.

The TOF gate isolates the ion bunch. Enable it with the TOF panel's Gate checkbox; the lower/upper value boxes default to 35 and 61 µs. Dragging an orange shaded region on the TOF panel sets the bounds live and the spectrum re-bins as you drag. The very first drag auto-arms the gate.

The timestamp gate restricts the spectrum to a chosen time window so you can watch how counts evolve over the run -- exactly like the old Data Viewer. Its Gate checkbox and value boxes live on the Timestamp panel, and its shaded region is deepskyblue. Crucially, the TOF and timestamp histograms keep showing all events; only the spectrum is filtered. The gate values are in the displayed timestamp units (Seconds / Minutes / ...) and are converted to absolute seconds at filter time.

items: Enabling a gate triggers a full replot that arms the live fast path; disabling it instantly hides the shaded region and fast-updates the spectrum.
The TOF gate is applied strictly (events strictly inside the bounds); the timestamp gate is inclusive of its end points.
Both gates can be set by typing into the value boxes -- the shaded region follows the typed numbers.

pa-tof-time-gate.text: The rest-frame frequency seen by the moving ion (used when you view the spectrum in Frequency mode while gating) follows the Doppler relation:

pa-tof-time-gate.name: doppler-seen
pa-tof-time-gate.caption: Rest-frame frequency seen by the ion for anti-collinear (DENIS default) and collinear geometries.

pa-tof-time-gate.text: The gate SpanSelectors deliberately run with blitting off. With blitting a visible selection ran a nested synchronous canvas redraw that could re-enter during a right-click menu and crash the renderer; without it the cheap TOF/timestamp figures repaint via coalesced draws while the spectrum stays smooth on its own numpy fast path.

pa-tof-time-gate.caption: The orange TOF SpanSelector dragged across the ion bunch on the TOF panel, with the Spectrum panel beneath re-binning live to the gated events.

pa-digit-stepping.text: The numeric value boxes used by the HFS model parameters support digit-aware stepping: click on a digit and the Up/Down arrows step by that digit's place value, so you can nudge a centroid by ones, tens, or hundreds without retyping.

rows: Highlights the single digit under the cursor.
Step the value by the place value (power of ten) of the highlighted digit, then re-highlight the same place.
Move the highlight to the previous/next digit (skipping the decimal point and sign).
Confirm the typed value, staying in the same field.
Copy / paste the numeric value (non-numeric paste is ignored).

pa-digit-stepping.text: Stepping by the digit's place value means: with the hundreds digit highlighted, Up adds 100; with the first decimal highlighted, it adds 0.1. The math is simply:

pa-digit-stepping.name: transition-frequency
pa-digit-stepping.caption: (Catalog placeholder -- the stepping itself just adds steps x 10^power, where power is the place value of the highlighted digit.)

items: The box shows a gold focus border while it has keyboard focus.
The scroll wheel only steps the value when the box is focused, so scrolling the surrounding panel never accidentally changes a parameter.

pa-digit-stepping.text: These shortcuts mirror the application-wide clipboard handling on numeric fields -- see [[clipboard-shortcuts]].

pa-xaxis-modes.text: The X-axis drop-down in Plot Options selects the horizontal axis of the spectrum. It converts the binned data between the lab frame (volts) and the rest frame (frequency) on the fly.

rows: Scanning voltage mapped through the CalSet -> CalReadback table.
Cooler voltage minus the calibrated scanning voltage (net beam energy).

pa-xaxis-modes.text: The Doppler conversion uses each run's cooler voltage, laser setpoint, isotope mass, harmonic, and the transition offset. The geometry is hard-coded to anti-collinear:

pa-xaxis-modes.name: doppler-seen
pa-xaxis-modes.caption: Rest-frame frequency seen by the moving ion; Pre-Analysis always uses the anti-collinear branch.

pa-xaxis-modes.text: Plot Options carries the energy levels (E lower, E upper in cm⁻¹) and the laser Harmonic that drive the conversion. Two read-only labels report the derived Transition (= E upper − E lower) and Fundamental (= Transition / harmonic, i.e. the laser setpoint wavenumber).

When the effective bin domain is Frequency the combo is restricted to Wavenumber and Frequency only -- a single frequency-bin centre has no clean inverse back to volts, so Voltage / Calibrated voltage / Calibrated beam energy are hidden. The bin domain itself follows the axis: choosing Frequency or Wavenumber bins in MHz, while the voltage-family axes keep raw-DV-step binning. See [[pa-binning]].

pa-xaxis-modes.caption: The same spectrum shown in Voltage mode and in Frequency mode, with the X-axis drop-down expanded showing all five entries.

pa-plot-options.text: The Plot Options group in the left column holds the physics parameters and display switches that control how every run is drawn. Without an override, each file uses its own header values.

rows: Transition energy levels feeding the Doppler conversion; the Transition and Fundamental labels are derived from them.
Atomic number (1-118) and mass number (1-300), with an auto isotope label and a mass looked up from the periodictable database.
Atomic mass for the Doppler shift; read-only and auto-filled from Z/A unless you tick Override to type a custom value (e.g. an AME2020 mass not in the database).
PMT-channel tickboxes 1, 2, 3, 4, and DC; default 3 & 4. All histograms are gated by the ticked channels.
Scale each run to unit peak height.

pa-plot-options.text: Cooler (V) and Laser (cm⁻¹) each have an enable tickbox, a value box, and a down-arrow auto-fill button. When the tick is off, every file uses its own header value; when on, the single typed value is applied to all files. The down-arrow fills the box from the currently selected file.
Edit Plot opens the shared plot editor, with the TOF and timestamp figures available as extra figures to style. See [[plot-editor]].

The full binning widget is intentionally hidden in this sidebar (the preview binning follows the display axis and defaults to per-scan-step). The only visible binning control is the Bin: N × step spin in the Spectrum header. The hidden settings still save/load in YAML. See [[pa-binning]].

pa-binning.text: The Pre-Analysis preview bins per scan step by default: one bin per native DAC voltage step (or its Doppler-shifted frequency equivalent), with no error bars — reproducing the legacy Data Viewer exactly. The spectrum is drawn as a step plot, and the header Bin: N × step spin groups N adjacent steps into one bin (count-weighted centers, summed counts) when more smoothing is wanted.

A uniform ("Auto") frequency grid at roughly one-step width sits exactly at the aliasing point: depending on where the grid falls, some bins swallow two scan steps and show doubled counts while their neighbours show none. Binning on the native steps cannot alias — every step is its own bin. The Analysis Source block defaults to the same definition; see [[an-source-block]].
Effective Bin Mode Follows the Axis

items: Frequency or Wavenumber axis → events are binned in MHz per scan step (clstools' Compute_WL gives each event a rest-frame frequency; DENIS groups events by their native DV step and takes the mean frequency per step).
Voltage-family axes (Voltage / Calibrated voltage / Calibrated beam energy) → raw-DV-step binning that matches the old Data Viewer.

pa-binning.text: Pre-Analysis shares the same compute_binned routine as the Analysis Source block, so a spectrum you read here matches what the fitter sees.
The full binning widget is built but hidden in the sidebar. Its objects still serialize to YAML, so a saved Pre-Analysis preserves these values:

pa-binning.code:
BIN_DEFINITIONS = ("Auto", "Fixed bin count",
                   "Fixed bin width", "Per scan step")
YERR_MODES = ("None", "Poisson sqrt(y+1)",
              "Poisson sqrt(y)", "Model-based")
DEFAULT_PA_BIN_DEFINITION = "Per scan step"   # preview
DEFAULT_BIN_DEFINITION    = "Per scan step"   # Analysis fits

pa-binning.text: Back-compatibility: a save file written before the bin-definition key existed reloads with Auto, reproducing its original behaviour — only fresh tabs and new Source blocks get the per-scan-step default. Because frequency binning has no clean inverse to volts, switching the bin domain to Frequency restricts the X-axis combo to Wavenumber and Frequency. See [[pa-xaxis-modes]].

pa-gate-fastpath.text: This page explains why dragging the [[pa-tof-time-gate|TOF or timestamp gate]] feels instant rather than triggering a full re-bin. It is background mechanics: there are no controls here, only a fast path DENIS arms automatically when the view is simple enough.
When the fast path is active

The fast path arms only for exactly one plain checked, loaded run — not a merged spectrum and not a virtual split. Merged spectra have no per-event arrays to re-histogram, and a split carries a permanent raw-voltage gate the in-memory path does not model. Any other view (two runs, a merge, a split) leaves the fast cache empty and gate drags fall back to the debounced re-bin.

items: A full replot is scheduled via a short debounce timer; a queued full replot always wins over a stray light schedule so it can never be downgraded.

Toggling the TOF/timestamp gate on forces a full replot (it rebuilds the gate selector and re-arms the cache); toggling it off hides the gate rectangle and runs only the spectrum fast update, so removing a gate is also instant.
When the single eligible run is drawn, DENIS caches the per-event coordinate, the per-event TOF/timestamp/TDC columns, the ungated bin edges, and the spectrum line object.

It self-checks by re-histogramming the ungated grid in numpy and requiring bit-exact equality with clstools' compute_binned. If the counts differ at all, the cache is discarded and the slow path is used.

On each gate move it re-applies the live PMT, TOF and timestamp masks, re-histograms in numpy (~1 ms), and blits only the spectrum line onto a cached static background — versus roughly 185 ms for a full re-bin plus figure redraw.

pa-gate-fastpath.text: The cache is built on the canonical ungated bin grid, not the currently gated view. A TOF or timestamp gate can empty the extreme bins; binning on the gated grid would narrow it permanently, so removing the gate later could never restore the missing bins. Re-binning ungated makes every gate a strict subset of the same grid.

The TOF gate is matched strictly (min < t < max) and the timestamp gate inclusively ([lo, hi]), exactly matching clstools' conventions so the fast histogram and the slow path agree. Any blit or cache problem silently drops to the safe dask redraw.

pa-hfs-overlay.text: The right-hand HFS Models panel lets you overlay one or more satlas2 hyperfine-structure models on the spectrum to eyeball constants before committing to a fit. Each model is a collapsible, checkable panel; the overlay updates live as you drag sliders.

rows: Append a new model panel (light colours cycle black, red, green, purple; each model also carries a neon dark-mode colour).
Copy each ticked model with a “(copy)” name suffix.
Remove ticked models. This is the one undoable action — Ctrl+Z restores them.

pa-hfs-overlay.text: Adding and duplicating are not undoable; only Remove checked pushes onto the undo stack. Tick a model panel's title checkbox to mark it before duplicating or removing.

The header row carries the model name, a colour button (opening the same dual light + dark colour dialog as the file list), a line-style combo (Solid, Dashed, Dotted, Dash-dot) and an opacity slider. Below it, nuclear spins I, Jl, Ju (defaults 3.5 / 4.5 / 5.5) and then one row per fit parameter, each with a value box, a slider, and a “…” button that opens a limits dialog.

Fix Al/Au locks the lower constant to a typed ratio (Al = ratio × Au); editing either value drives the other. Fix Bl/Bu does the same for the quadrupole pair. When you import a model into the Analysis tab, those locks set the constants' fixed flag 1:1.

pa-hfs-overlay.name: hfs-energy
pa-hfs-overlay.caption: The hyperfine level shift satlas2 evaluates for each F; the model is built with racah=True and drawn in MHz, then projected onto the current display x-axis.

pa-hfs-overlay.text: Quantum numbers are validated (non-negative half-integers) before any model is built; an invalid I/Jl/Ju simply skips drawing. The full panel state, including slider ranges and the ratio locks, round-trips through the [[pa-save-load|YAML]] under the models key.

pa-hfs-overlay.caption: An HFS Models panel with one model expanded: header (name/color/style/opacity), I/Jl/Ju spins, the Al/Au/Bl/Bu rows with Fix Al/Au and Fix Bl/Bu ratio locks, the value+slider+limits rows, and the Peak Amplitudes section collapsed below.

pa-peak-amplitudes.text: Inside each [[pa-hfs-overlay|HFS model panel]] the collapsible Peak Amplitudes section exposes one row per allowed hyperfine transition, so you can override individual component heights instead of letting Racah intensities alone set them.

Whenever I, Jl or Ju change, the rows are rebuilt from a fresh satlas2.HFS(..., racah=True). Each row shows the transition label and satlas2's verbatim Racah amplitude in grey parentheses (e.g. (0.42)). These values are not normalized to sum to one: the absolute scale is degenerate with the model's global Scale, so rescaling would only obscure the satlas2 internal values you might cross-check against a reference.

rows: Use satlas2's Racah amplitude (the default; value box disabled).
Amplitude = ratio × another peak's effective amplitude; a sub-row shows the ratio spinbox and a target-peak combo.

pa-peak-amplitudes.text: At draw time, any Free or Linked override is resolved (Linked peaks reference the live amplitude of their target, falling back to its Racah value) and pushed into the satlas2 model's Amp<label> parameters before the curve is evaluated. With everything left on Racah, no overrides are applied.
The neighboring Show Labels checkbox annotates each component on the spectrum at its peak position, rotated 45°, with the transition label (e.g. 3→4) and a thin leader line in the model's color.

pa-scan-filtering.text: A scan is one full sweep of the voltage range. DENIS can drop individual low-quality scans from a run so they never reach binning or fitting. Exclusions live in a process-wide registry shared with the [[tab-analysis|Analysis tab]], so a filter set here applies to the same file there too.

Each raw event carries a monotonic Bunch index. The per-event scan index is bunch // bunches_per_scan, where the bunches-per-scan count comes from the ASDF's ScanningRanges, StepSize and BunchesPerChannel:

pa-scan-filtering.name: bunches-per-scan
pa-scan-filtering.caption: Total bunches per full scan. If the metadata is missing or degenerate this returns 0 and scan filtering is unavailable for that file.

pa-scan-filtering.text: Right-click a file row and choose Filter scans… (the label shows the current excluded count). The dialog lists every scan present in the file with these columns:

rows: Original scan index (gaps preserved for empty scans).
Start time relative to the file's first event.
Tick to keep the scan; clear to exclude it.

items: Check All / Uncheck All and Check Selected / Uncheck Selected act on highlighted rows (click, Shift-click for a range, Ctrl-click to toggle).
The Exclude rate < spinbox plus Apply unchecks every scan below a PMT-rate threshold (in Hz); it is additive and never re-checks anything you excluded by hand.
The PMT gate used for the per-scan rate comes from your current [[pa-plot-options|channel selection]] (default channels 3 and 4).

pa-scan-filtering.text: Alternatively, tick Show scans on the [[pa-spectrum-panels|Timestamp]] plot (active only when exactly one non-merged file is shown). Scan boundaries appear as vertical ticks — grey for included, red bands for excluded. Pan or zoom to a bad stretch and click Exclude scans in view to add every scan whose start time falls in the current x-range to the exclusion set; existing exclusions are preserved.

Internally a context manager (filter_data_for_binning) temporarily drops the excluded events before each Compute_Bins and restores the original data on exit, so the same loaded run can be re-used with no side effects. Exclusions serialize under the top-level scan_filters key in the [[pa-save-load|saved YAML]].

pa-scan-filtering.caption: The Filter scans dialog: per-scan table (Scan/Start/Dur/Events/PMT/Rate/Include) with the Check/Uncheck Selected buttons and the Exclude rate < threshold + Apply control.
The Timestamp plot with Show scans on: grey ticks for included scans, red-banded excluded scans, and the Exclude scans in view button.

pa-virtual-splits.text: Virtual splitting turns one parent ASDF into two virtual sub-runs without ever modifying the parent. Each side is described by a tiny .vasdf YAML sidecar that points at the parent plus a raw-voltage gate, which you can then load in either the Pre-Analysis or [[tab-analysis|Analysis]] tab.
Open it from Edit › Split File…. It is standalone — no open project required.

items: Click Open ASDF… to load a parent run. Its raw scanning-voltage events are drawn as a histogram.
Place the cut: drag the red line on the plot, or type a value into Cut at raw voltage:. The two sides are shaded blue (left) and orange (right), with a live left/right event count below the plot.
Fill in each side's form: Source ID, Cooler (V), Laser (cm⁻¹) and an optional Comment. Source IDs default to <run>_A and <run>_B and the cooler/laser default to the parent's values.
Click Save Split Files… and pick a path for each side.

pa-virtual-splits.text: Both sides need a non-empty Source ID and the two IDs must differ — the editor refuses to save otherwise. Default file names are <parent_base>_<suffix>.vasdf next to the parent ASDF.

You can also click Open existing .vasdf… to re-edit a split: the editor loads its parent automatically and, if it finds the adjoining sibling sidecar, pre-fills both sides so Save overwrites both files in place.

pa-virtual-splits.code:
write_vasdf(path, parent_path, source_id, label,
            lo, hi,  # raw-voltage gate for this side
            metadata_override={"cooler_v": ..., "laser_sp": ...,
                               "comment": ...})
pa-virtual-splits.caption: Each side is one descriptor. Left side gets [dv_min, cut]; right side gets [cut, dv_max]. The parent ASDF is never touched.

pa-virtual-splits.text: Loading a .vasdf creates a SplitFileEntry whose filepath is the sidecar itself; it carries the [lo, hi] raw-voltage gate as a permanent filter applied at every binning consumer. Because a split shares its parent's calibration and cooler arrays, splits are skipped on the [[pa-calibrations|Calibrations]] and [[pa-cooler-voltage|Cooler Voltage]] diagnostic tabs and are not eligible for the [[pa-gate-fastpath|gate-drag fast path]].

pa-virtual-splits.caption: The Split File editor: raw-voltage histogram with the draggable red cut line, blue/orange shaded sides, the per-side metadata forms (Source ID/Cooler/Laser/Comment), and the left/right counts line.

pa-merging.text: Merging co-bins several loaded runs into a single synthetic spectrum entry that plots, overlays models, and exports like an ordinary run. Pre-Analysis and Analysis use the same merge backend, so the results are identical.

Tick at least two loaded, non-merged runs and click Merge Checked. With fewer than two eligible runs DENIS prompts you to select more. The shared Merge Dialog opens with its Merge domain defaulted from your current [[pa-xaxis-modes|x-axis]]: viewing in Frequency or Wavenumber defaults to a frequency merge, otherwise voltage.

rows: Co-bins raw lab-frame DAC voltage. Use when the runs share cooler and laser. The merged spectrum needs explicit cooler/laser/mass/harmonic to be Doppler-shifted at fit time.
Doppler-shifts each file to the rest frame with its own cooler/laser before binning, so the merged axis is rest-frame MHz directly.

pa-merging.name: doppler-seen
pa-merging.caption: In a frequency merge each file's events are shifted to the rest frame (anti-collinear geometry) before co-binning.

pa-merging.text: A frequency merge can additionally apply any per-file [[pa-centroid-offset|manual centroid offsets]] you have set, threaded into the same point where the dialog applies its GP centroid alignment.

Accepting the dialog produces a synthetic MergedFileEntry in the file list. Right-click it for View…, Edit… and Export ASDF… — the same trio the Analysis Source block exposes, so you can write a DENIS-merged ASDF and reload it as a single run. The merged x/y arrays are stored inline in the [[pa-save-load|saved YAML]].

For a frequency merge the dialog's cooler/laser/mass metadata fields are hidden and the saved entry stores them as None — the rest-frame axis is already baked in, so persisting stale pre-fills would misrepresent your intent.

pa-merging.caption: The Merge Dialog showing the Merge domain combo (voltage/frequency) and bin-step controls, with the resulting synthetic merged entry visible in the Pre-Analysis file list behind it.

pa-centroid-offset.text: A per-file centroid offset is a manual MHz shift you assign to a single run to align its absolute frequency calibration with the others before a [[pa-merging|frequency-domain merge]].
Right-click a file row and choose Set centroid offset…. The menu label shows the current value when one is set (for example Set centroid offset… (+12.50 MHz)). A small dialog takes the offset in MHz.
This action appears only on real source files, not on merged entries: a merged spectrum's x-axis was fixed at merge time, so there is no consumer for an offset on it.

When you run Merge Checked, any non-zero per-file offsets are collected into a map and passed to the Merge Dialog. In a frequency merge they are applied at the same stage as the dialog's GP centroid alignment (the two are additive), shifting each file's rest-frame axis before co-binning. A voltage merge does not consume the offset. Offsets round-trip in the [[pa-save-load|saved YAML]] under each file's centroid_offset_mhz key.

pa-calibrations.text: The Calibrations tab shows three stacked diagnostics of the scanning-voltage DAC, all plotted against the requested set voltage. Each checked, non-split run contributes one colored curve.

rows: Measured voltage vs requested — overall voltage response.
Systematic offset and drift of the supply across the scan range.
Step-to-step change in readback — step uniformity / non-linearity.

pa-calibrations.text: The curves are built from each run's CalSet and CalReadback arrays. The Info button at the top of the tab opens a short explanation of each pane. No mean/std/SEM statistics are computed here — those live on the separate [[pa-cooler-voltage|Cooler Voltage]] tab.
Virtual splits are skipped on this tab. A split shares its parent's calibration arrays, so plotting it would only duplicate the parent's curves under a different label.
The calibration fit, alerts, and overrides

Each run's CalSet → CalReadback table is fitted by DENIS itself on every load (so results do not depend on the installed clstools build), and by default nothing is dropped. A run whose calibration outliers would actually move its centroid gets a blinking ! badge on its file row, in both Pre-Analysis and Analysis. Click it: you get the outlier count, the centroid shift in MHz, and the axis tilt across the scan, with Open calibration… / Keep as-is — either way the blinking stops for good, and the acknowledgement is saved with the project.

Right-click a run → Calibration… for the full diagnostic: the calibration curve with the uncorrected and in-force polynomials overlaid, residuals against both, and the headline cost in MHz. You can exclude points (click them, drop the first N settling points, or an n·σ residual cut — prefer the iterative form), tick Force zero intercept (p0 = 0) for a chain with no DC offset, borrow another run's calibration, or type coefficients directly. Calibration overview… triages every loaded run at once, worst first.

Overrides are a property of the file, live in a process-wide registry shared by every tab, and persist under the save file's top-level calibrations: key (acknowledgements under calibration_acks:) — siblings of scan_filters:. Every drop is recorded in the fit report and in merged files' per-run provenance.

pa-cooler-voltage.text: The Cooler Voltage tab diagnoses the stability of the cooler high voltage over the course of each run, using robust statistics that are not biased by occasional spikes.

items: Top — Cooler V (V) [raw]: per-event cooler voltage (Vrfq · VCoolDiv + VCoolOffset) in absolute volts, with a dashed line at the robust run average Vref. Runs above ~50k events are stride-decimated for responsive drawing.

Middle — Deviation from run average (V): the same data with Vref subtracted. Constant ±σ and ±3σ bands, a per-bin median deviation line (a rolling drift indicator), and dots marking individual spike samples beyond ±3σ (capped at 500 per run).
Bottom — Ripple amplitude (V): per-bin RMS (solid) and per-bin P95−P5 (dashed) over time, telling you whether the supply was stable across the whole run or only in places.

pa-cooler-voltage.name: robust-cooler-stats
pa-cooler-voltage.caption: V_ref is the median of the per-event cooler voltage; sigma_robust is the MAD-derived Gaussian sigma; a spike is any sample more than 3 sigma_robust from V_ref.

rows: Clamps the deviation pane's y-axis to ±4·σ (the robust sigma, 1.4826·MAD — immune to spikes) so normal ripple stays readable; uncheck to let it autoscale around spike dots.
Number of equal-width time bins for the per-bin median, RMS and P95−P5.

pa-cooler-voltage.text: A sortable per-run summary table above the panes reports Vref, σ, peak-to-peak, the spike count, the signed extremes, and σ converted to its approximate Doppler impact in MHz — so you can judge run health at a glance. The deviation pane carries a matching secondary y-axis in ≈Δν (MHz). The Info button explains each pane in full. As on the [[pa-calibrations|Calibrations]] tab, virtual splits are skipped because cooler stability is a parent-run property.

pa-cooler-voltage.caption: The Cooler Voltage tab: the raw, deviation (with sigma bands and spike dots) and ripple panes, plus the per-run status strip and the Clip y / Bins header controls.

pa-save-load.text: All Pre-Analysis state round-trips through YAML so you can reopen a session exactly as you left it. The tab's own state lives under a preanalysis key; multiple Pre-Analysis projects are stored as a projects list.

items: The file list (real ASDFs and loaded .vasdf splits both as plain {path, ...} entries; the sidecar path itself carries the split gate).
Merged entries, with their x/y arrays stored inline plus the merge metadata and source audit trail.

Plot options (x-axis, E lower/upper, harmonic, normalize, Z/A, mass override, channels, plot layout, dark mode, grid toggles), the TOF gate and TOF bin size, the timestamp gate, the cooler/laser overrides, the binning settings (including the step multiple), and all [[pa-hfs-overlay|HFS models]] — every file and model with both its light and dark colours.
Per-file [[pa-centroid-offset|centroid offsets]] under each file's centroid_offset_mhz.
[[pa-scan-filtering|Scan exclusions]] are serialized separately under the YAML's top-level scan_filters key.
Calibration overrides and acknowledged calibration warnings are serialized under the YAML's top-level calibrations and calibration_acks keys — see [[pa-calibrations]].

pa-save-load.text: On load, paths are normalized cross-platform (a POSIX path round-trips on Windows and vice versa). If any referenced data file no longer exists, the loader walks both the Pre-Analysis file lists and the Analysis Source file lists and offers a locate-or-skip flow:

items: scan_missing_paths collects the unique missing paths, Pre-Analysis first then Analysis projects in order.
Located files are remapped in place; skipped files are pruned from the in-memory config before it loads.
Synthetic merged:// paths are ignored — they are not on disk.

pa-save-load.text: Legacy keys are handled on load: an old single offset field maps onto E_upper with E_lower 0, and flat preanalysis.files[] saves (predating the multi-project container) are still read.

an-projects.text: The Analysis tab holds one fit per project, each in its own sub-tab. Click + Create Analysis Project and pick the kind of project from its drop-down menu; a permanent Isotope Shifts tab appears once any project exists.

The + Create Analysis Project button is a menu with two entries. Both build the identical Source -> Model -> Fitter -> Output pipeline; the only difference is how their fitted centroids are used downstream by the drift correction.

rows: The standard fit pipeline; the isotope you actually want to measure. Isotope shifts are computed from these centroids.
Tagged as a reference: its fitted centroids feed the Gaussian-process drift correction in the Isotope Shifts tab. Use for scans of a stable reference isotope taken throughout a campaign.

an-projects.text: On creation you are prompted for a project name (the default is Project_N for samples, Reference_N for references). Every new project is born with one each of Source, Model, Fitter, and Output blocks already in place, so you can start configuring immediately.

items: Rename — double-click the project tab to type a new name.

Convert — right-click the tab for Convert to Reference Project / Convert to Sample Project. This flips the kind in place, keeping all existing blocks and fits; the (Reference) suffix is added or removed accordingly.
Reorder — drag tabs along the bar (tabs are movable).
Close — the close (x) button removes a project. The Isotope Shifts tab cannot be closed.

an-projects.text: The Isotope Shifts tab is permanent and always kept last on the bar, even when you reorder or add projects. It is hidden only until the first project exists.
A whole-tab YAML save/load round-trips every project (its blocks and settings) plus the isotope-shift study. See [[an-save-load]].

an-pipeline.text: A project is a left-to-right pipeline of four colour-coded block types. You assemble it from + Add Block and reorder by dragging. Each block is a checkable group box: unchecking it disables the block and excludes it from the fit.

rows: Load ASDF/.vasdf files, gate, and bin into a spectrum
Build one satlas2 model bound to a Source
Choose mode, optimiser, statistic, sharing, constraints

an-pipeline.text: Every block carries the same header and frame controls:

items: Enable checkbox — the group-box title is checkable; uncheck to disable the block and drop it from the fit.
Name field — an editable line edit; the title reads <Type>: <name>.
Drag handle — the hamburger button (☰, tooltip Drag to reorder); dragging shows a blue vertical drop indicator at the insertion point.
Remove — the ✗ button removes the block.
Resizable width — drag the block's right edge (cursor changes near the edge) to widen or narrow it; width is remembered per project on save.

an-pipeline.text: Add blocks with + Add Block, whose menu offers Source, Model, Fitter, and Output. New projects start with one of each. The bottom Info button opens the in-app pipeline guide.

Use multiple blocks for composite fits — e.g. an HFS Model plus a Polynomial Model sharing the same Source for a sloping background, or several Source blocks for a [[an-multisource|multi-source]] simultaneous fit.

an-source-block.text: The Source block loads run files and produces a binned spectrum for the fit. It is organised into Files, Physics Parameters, Gates, Binning, Advanced Data Settings, an optional Cooler/Laser Override, and a preview toolbar.

items: + Add Files — browse for ASDF / .vasdf runs.
Import from Pre-Analysis — pick a Pre-Analysis project and pull its ticked files, physics parameters, gates, and cooler/laser overrides in one click.
Merge Selected — combine the checked files into a single synthetic spectrum (see [[an-merge-dialog]]).
Check all — a tri-state master checkbox above the list; clicking forces every file checked or unchecked at once (the square mixed state shows when only some are ticked).

rows: Read-only; auto-filled from the IUPAC/AME table on Z/A change. Tick Override to keep a typed value across edits
Lower/upper atomic energy levels; their difference defines the rest-frame transition used for Doppler binning

items: TOF gate — on by default, bounds in µs (default 38–44) to select the ion bunch.
PMT — channels 1–4 (3 and 4 ticked by default) plus a DC channel.
V gate — voltage window [min, max] on the raw DV column.
F gate (MHz) — frequency window on the Doppler-corrected frequency (entered in MHz, stored in Hz).
Noise filter — max events per timestamp, 0 disables (removes noise bursts).

rows: bin midpoint vs mean event frequency (frequency mode)
None, Poisson sqrt(y+1), Poisson sqrt(y), Model-based
sqrt(y+1) is the default and recommended; see equation below
Frequency needs mass+levels+harmonic; Raw Voltage groups by unique DV and ignores bin count/width
Per scan step, Auto, Fixed bin count, Fixed bin width
Per scan step is the default: one bin per native voltage step, immune to uniform-grid aliasing. Auto (clstools' uniform grid) can alias against the step spacing — the binning dialog flags it
active for Fixed bin width; realised width may drift (warns above ~5%)
groups N adjacent native steps into one bin (Per scan step and Raw Voltage)

an-source-block.name: model-yerr
an-source-block.caption: Model-based yerr: satlas2 recomputes the per-bin error from the model's expected counts each iteration, removing the downward bias of sqrt(y). The default Poisson sqrt(y+1) avoids the empty-bin zero-error pathology.

items: Cal. order — polynomial order (1–3, default 1 linear) for the LCR-voltage calibration applied at load.
Cooler corr. — pbp (point-by-point, tracks drift) or mean (run-averaged) cooler-voltage subtraction.
Ref. shift [MHz] — additive offset to the reference frequency defining x = 0 (stored in Hz at the backend).

an-source-block.name: lcr-calibration
an-source-block.caption: LCR-voltage calibration applied at file load (Cal. order chooses the polynomial degree).

an-source-block.name: cooler-correction
an-source-block.caption: Per-event voltage after cooler-drift subtraction (Cooler corr. mode chooses pbp vs mean cooler voltage).

an-source-block.text: Cooler / Laser Override and the Toolbar

Tick Cooler / Laser Override to force every file to use one cooler voltage and/or laser setpoint instead of each ASDF file's metadata. The bottom toolbar offers Preview (quick spectrum look, with prev/next file navigation), Meta (run metadata), Run Stats (experimental parameters vs run number), and Binning (a three-tab health check: a per-run Summary with occupancy columns, a Run detail view with bin edges, warnings, and a V↔MHz scale strip, and a Compare heatmap of all runs on one grid).

Per-file binning overrides are limited to binning keys only (bin_mode, x_column, yerr_mode, xerr_mode, bin_definition, bin_count, bin_width_mhz, step_multiple). Physics, gates, mass, and overrides always stay at the Source level.

an-model-block.text: A Model block builds one satlas2 model bound to a chosen Source block. The Type drop-down picks the function; for HFS, the parameter table and Racah/sidepeak settings shape the hyperfine fit.

Type offers HFS (default), Voigt, Skewed Voigt, Exponential Decay, Piecewise Constant, and Polynomial. Source selects which Source block provides the data. Two seed buttons populate the table: Import from Pre-Analysis pulls I, J, A, B, and centroid from the Pre-Analysis HFS overlay; Retrieve Last Fit loads the previous iteration's fitted values as new initial guesses.

items: Racah — checked by default; enforces Racah intensity ratios fixed by angular momentum. Uncheck to fit individual peak amplitudes freely (the Show Peak Amplitudes table then becomes active).
Sidepeaks — N charge-exchange sidepeaks (0–20, 0 disabled), an Offset [MHz], and a Poisson distribution toggle.

an-model-block.text: The HFS peak-shape combo is hidden: satlas2 0.1.10 supports Voigt only for HFS. Use the dedicated Skewed Voigt model type for asymmetric peaks.

The central table has five columns: Parameter, Value, Bounds (min, max), Mode, and Expression. There is no separate Vary checkbox — the Mode combo is the single source of truth for whether a parameter varies and what constrains it.

rows: Floats freely (vary = True). This is the only mode that varies the parameter
Locked equal to another parameter (auto-generates an expression)
A scaled multiple of another parameter
An additive offset from another parameter
A free-form expression you type in the Expression cell

an-model-block.text: Equal / Ratio / Offset auto-generate the expression for you; the cell is live-validated with red-tint feedback as you type. HFS metadata I, Jl, Ju are never fittable (fixed by physics). Model-block expressions reference bare local names; see [[an-expressions]].

an-model-block.name: hfs-energy
an-model-block.caption: Hyperfine level energy shift built from the fitted A and B constants (Casimir factor C).
