an-fitter.text: The Fitter block decides how sources combine and how the fit runs. The two radios at the top — Separate (per file) (default) and Simultaneous — govern which other controls appear.

items: Separate (per file) — fits each file independently, in parallel; each run gets its own parameter copy. See [[an-multisource]].
Simultaneous — fits all files at once with one satlas2 Fitter, and reveals Parameter Sharing, Advanced Constraints, and Common Grid.

rows: leastsq, least_squares, slsqp, emcee, nelder, powell, cobyla
leastsq is the fast Levenberg–Marquardt default; emcee samples an MCMC posterior
sets the cost function; Poisson LLH is best for low counts
scales uncertainties by √(reduced χ²); forced off for likelihood fits

an-fitter.caption: How the Statistics combo maps to the fit call (get_fitter_config / fitting.py).

an-fitter.name: scale-covariance
an-fitter.caption: Effect of Scale covariance: parameter errors are multiplied by sqrt of the reduced chi-square.

items: Parameter Sharing (simultaneous) — tick a bare parameter (e.g. Al) and choose Model (share across same-named models) or All (share across every source).
Advanced Constraints (simultaneous) — full-name expressions on individual cross-run/cross-model targets; see [[an-expressions]].
Show Priors → Gaussian Priors table — each prior adds a penalty term.
MCMC settings (Method = emcee) — walkers, steps, burn/thin, and optional auto-convergence on autocorrelation time.

an-fitter.name: gaussian-prior
an-fitter.caption: A Gaussian prior adds this penalty for a parameter's departure from its prior value.

an-fitter.text: In Separate mode, Gaussian Priors and Advanced Constraints are silently ignored (the pre-fit validator warns about constraints). They take effect only in Simultaneous mode.

▶ Run Fit starts the fit. Find Parameters opens the multi-start Auto-Fitter to seed parameters; ■ Stop cancels a running fit; ↶ Revert restores model parameters to their pre-fit values. See [[an-autofitter]].
The Auto-Fitter is a multi-start parallel leastsq sweep — many perturbed copies of your current parameters fitted in parallel and ranked by χ2. See [[an-autofitter]].

an-output-block.text: The Output block selects which artifacts a fit produces. It groups into Reports, Fit Plots, Tracker Plots, Diagnostics, and Iteration. All toggles below default on except where noted.

items: Fit report (text) (on) — a text report with parameter values, uncertainties, and fit statistics.
Show correlations (on) with a min threshold (default 0.1) — pairs below the threshold are hidden.
Parameters CSV (on) and Metadata CSV (on) — tables of fitted parameters and per-run fit metadata.

rows: type: ToF only / ToF + spectrum / ToF + spectrum + fit
normalised residual panel below the fit
drops y ≤ 0 markers/error bars from the plot only; fit unaffected
overlays individual model components (per-component checkboxes appear)

an-output-block.text: Fit values on plot adds an on-plot values box ("Name = value ± err", two significant error digits) fed by a per-parameter picker tree; the values are stored in the fit's .npz so the Results tab re-renders them verbatim. The Plot Options… button under the Fit Plots group opens the per-plot-type styling dialog — global rcParams, the fit plot's shade-under-fit and values-box size, tracker / walk / correlation / chi-square-map styles, and the isotope-shift plot.

items: Tracker Plots (Separate mode) — plot selected parameters vs Run number or Start time. Only meaningful for multi-run separate fits.
Diagnostics — Chi-square map (any method), Correlation plot and Walk plot (emcee only), and Confidence bands (emcee, with a Samples count, default 200).
Iteration — Auto increments iter_001, iter_002, …; Manual uses a custom Label.

an-output-block.text: Update iteration (formerly Re-apply outputs) regenerates the output files for the last fit's iteration using the current toggles, without re-running the fit — useful when you realise you forgot (say) ToF plots. It updates the existing iteration folder in place rather than spawning a new one, and requires a fit to have run this session. Newly-ticked MCMC walk / correlation plots are rebuilt from the saved chains; only the chi-square map and confidence bands need a true re-run — the dialog lists anything it could not regenerate.
Tracker plots and weighted CSVs only generate for multi-run results. Output files land under <output_root>/analysis/<project>/iter_NNN/ and then surface in the Results tab.

an-expressions.text: Parameter constraints are written as expressions in two distinct namespaces. A pure validator checks them live as you type and again in a blocking pre-fit pass before any heavy lifting.

rows: always; lowered to full lmfit names per source at fit time

an-expressions.text: Bare model expressions are rewritten to one full name per source before the fit. The full-name scheme is shown below; note the Bkg_p0 background parameter is remapped to a separate sub-model.

an-expressions.code:
full_param_name = Run_<id>___<safe_model>___<param>
#   safe_model = block name with non-alphanumerics -> '_'
#   Bkg_p0 is remapped to  Run_<id>___<safe_model>_bkg___p0
# example: Al * 0.5  in HFS_1 of run 7164
#   lowers to  Run_7164___HFS_1___Al * 0.5
an-expressions.caption: Full lmfit parameter naming (naming.py).

items: Parse errors — malformed expressions.
Name resolution — unknown identifiers (only this model's bare names, or existing full targets, plus numpy/math builtins like sqrt, exp, pi resolve).
Namespace misuse — a full Run_X___ name in a model cell, or a bare name in an Advanced Constraint, is an error.
Self-reference — an expression referencing its own parameter.
Vary + expression conflict — a parameter set to vary that also has an expression (lmfit silently sets vary off): a warning.
Dependency cycles — chains of constraints that loop back on themselves.

an-expressions.text: Live per-cell validation gives instant red-tint feedback and only does the cheap checks (parse + name resolution). The full set — cycles, cross-config consistency, vary/expr conflicts — runs in the blocking pre-fit dialog: errors must be fixed before the fit starts, while warnings can be acknowledged to continue.

In Separate mode, every non-empty Advanced Constraint is reported as a warning and then ignored — those expressions only take effect in Simultaneous mode. Fitter-block expressions take precedence over Parameter Sharing and model-block expressions for the same target (last-write-wins).

an-multisource.text: How multiple files and Model blocks combine depends on the [[an-fitter|Fitter]] block's Fit Mode. The two modes differ in whether each file is its own fit or all files share one fitter.

Each checked file is fitted independently with its own parameter copy. Fits run in parallel across a process pool (capped by the [[performance-settings|max cores]] setting), with a blended progress bar that combines per-run completion with each worker's inner iteration fraction. Tracker plots are meaningful here because they compare runs. Parameter Sharing, Advanced Constraints, and priors do not apply in this mode.
Every source is added to one satlas2 Fitter and fitted together. The following are then applied, in order:

items: Parameter Sharing — ticked bare names go to shareModelParams (Mode = Model) or shareParams (Mode = All).
Model-block expressions — lowered from bare names to a full name for every source.
Advanced Constraints — full-name fitter expressions applied last, so they win for any shared target (last-write-wins).
Gaussian priors — applied to their full-name targets.
Optionally a Common Grid re-bins all sources onto one shared x grid.

an-multisource.text: The Advanced Constraints and Parameter Sharing tables auto-populate from the union of bare parameters across enabled Model blocks, and their target rows come from the files checked in the first enabled Source block — the same sources the fitter actually instantiates.

In both modes, results are ordered by natural run-number sort (numeric runs ascending, then non-numeric labels such as merged names) so the fit report, per-run CSVs, and saved figures all follow the same order rather than nondeterministic completion order.

an-autofitter.text: The Auto-Fitter is a fast way to find good starting parameters when your initial guesses are poor. Click Find Parameters on the [[an-fitter|Fitter block]] to open it; it generates many slightly-perturbed copies of your current parameters and runs a quick fit on each in parallel, then ranks them by χ2.
The window title is Auto-Fitter; the button that opens it is labelled Find Parameters (with a crosshair icon). The engine is a multi-start parallel leastsq sweep.

For each start, every varying parameter j is drawn from a Gaussian centred on its current value cj, with a standard deviation set by the Spread control. The very first start always reuses your original guess unperturbed, so the sweep can never do worse than where you began. Only non-fixed, non-expression parameters are perturbed — fixed parameters and expression-tied ones are left exactly as the [[an-model-block|Model block]] defines them.

an-autofitter.name: auto-fitter-spread
an-autofitter.caption: Per-parameter perturbation: s is the Spread fraction; the +1 floor keeps near-zero parameters from collapsing to a zero spread.

rows: Number of perturbed starting points (each is one leastsq fit).
Perturbation width as a fraction of each parameter value. 0.30 = roughly ±30% of the value.
1 to detected CPU count, default CPU−2
Worker processes used to run starts in parallel.
Run a fresh round from your original initial guesses.
Re-seed a new round around the selected best result, with the Spread halved (floor 0.02).

an-autofitter.text: As starts complete, the Results (ranked by χ2) table updates live with the top 10, showing Rank, χ2, χ2_red, and a compact Parameters summary. The plot follows the current best automatically; click any row to pin that result and inspect it (double-click a row for the full parameter list). The Show checkboxes toggle Data, Total fit, and Model components. Expand Show Core Activity for a per-core progress bar that turns green as each core finishes its assigned starts.

an-autofitter.caption: Auto-Fitter window mid-sweep: the Starts/Spread/Cores row, the χ²-ranked results table, the live fit plot, and the expanded Core Activity panel.

an-autofitter.text: Select the row you want and click Accept Selected. The chosen parameters are written back into the Model blocks' value fields as a single Auto-Fit Accept command, so one [[undo-redo|Undo]] reverses all of them at once. The Auto-Fitter does not run the real fit — accepting only seeds new initial guesses, after which you click Run Fit normally. In simultaneous mode the sweep respects the Fitter block's [[an-multisource|parameter sharing]], and only the first source's accepted values are pushed to the blocks.
If no parameters are varying, the Auto-Fitter warns and does nothing — set at least one parameter's Mode to Free in the [[an-model-block|Model block]] first.

an-merge-dialog.text: The Merge dialog combines several runs of the same isotope into one higher-statistics synthetic spectrum. In the [[an-source-block|Source block]], tick at least two loaded, non-merged files and click Merge Selected to open the Merge Runs dialog. The result becomes a single merged entry in the file list that behaves like a normal source for fitting, viewing, and export.
The Merge domain combo chooses how runs are co-binned:

items: voltage — runs are histogrammed on a common raw DAC-voltage axis. The merged spectrum keeps no per-event Doppler information, so it carries merge-level Doppler metadata (cooler V, laser setpoint, mass, harmonic) that is used to project the voltage axis to rest-frame MHz at fit time. See [[physics-voltage-projection]].

frequency — each file is independently Doppler-shifted to the rest frame using its own cooler voltage and laser setpoint before binning, so files with different setpoints land on the same MHz axis. Requires non-zero ref_freq, positive mass, and positive harmonic in the Source config.

an-merge-dialog.text: The default domain follows the Source block: frequency when the physics parameters are set, voltage otherwise (or when bin mode is Raw Voltage). When you merge from the Pre-Analysis tab the default follows that tab's current x-axis instead (see [[pa-merging]]).

an-merge-dialog.name: doppler-seen
an-merge-dialog.caption: In a frequency merge, each file's lab-frame frequency is shifted to the rest frame before co-binning (anti-collinear vs collinear).

rows: Auto uses the median Δx across the source files; Manual exposes a step spinbox (default 20, range 0.1–1000) in V or MHz to match the domain.
pbp (per-bunch-pair) or mean; inherited from the Source config by default.

Subtract the per-file GP centroid correction from each file's MHz axis before histogramming. Enabled only when the [[an-reference-gp|Reference Correction (GP)]] panel has supplied corrections for the files; with partial coverage it is offered unchecked with a warning.
Cooler V, Laser setpoint (cm⁻¹), Mass (amu), Harmonic (1–32, default 2). Shown only for voltage merges; pre-filled from the source files' means (or the Source override when its tick is on).
Per-field Auto / per-run / Custom choices used when exporting the merge to ASDF.

an-merge-dialog.text: The Merge dialog is essentially identical to the Pre-Analysis merge dialog — same domain combo, bin-step controls, and Doppler metadata. See [[pa-merging|Merging Runs (Pre-Analysis)]] for a screenshot and walkthrough of the same controls.
Preview, accept, and managing merged entries

Click Preview Merge to open a pop-out plot of the faded per-run spectra under the solid merged curve before committing. On OK the merged entry appears in the Source file list with a diamond marker. Its hamburger menu offers Edit… (re-open this dialog with all settings restored), View… (a multi-tab Spectrum/TOF/Info viewer), Export ASDF… (write a DENIS-merged ASDF you can reload as a normal run), and Remove.

A voltage-merged entry fitted in Frequency mode shows a warning badge: it can only be projected to MHz if its merge-level Doppler metadata is complete. Manual per-file centroid offsets are MHz and are silently ignored by a voltage merge — switch to a frequency merge to apply them.

an-isotope-shifts.text: The Isotope Shifts sub-tab is permanent and always sits last in the Analysis tab strip (it appears once any project exists). It pulls fitted centroids from your [[an-projects|sample projects]], combines runs, applies systematic and correction uncertainties, and produces a shift table and comparison plot. The left panel is split into a Setup tab and a Reference Correction (GP) tab; the right panel holds Plot, Table, and Log.

Each row is one isotope, with columns Sel., Project, Label, A, Runs, Centroid (MHz), Stat. Err., and Ref. Use + Add Row / - Remove Row to edit it manually, or Refresh from Projects to scan all sample projects and auto-populate rows (reference projects are excluded — they feed the GP corrector instead). The Ref radio marks the reference isotope (exactly one). Pick the reference under [[res-tree|Settings]]; here the first added row is marked reference by default.

items: Runs: choose Weighted Average to combine every successful run of that project, or pick a single run number.
Centroid / Stat. Err. are read-only and filled from cached fit results (or loaded from the latest iter_NNN on disk if not in memory).

an-isotope-shifts.text: A weighted average uses inverse-variance weights and inflates the uncertainty by the Birge ratio when the runs scatter more than their fit errors imply.

A collapsible Run preview panel under the table shows the highlighted row's selected run — data, fitted curve, and the reduced χ2 in the title — so you can sanity-check a centroid before it enters the shift.

an-isotope-shifts.name: weighted-average
an-isotope-shifts.caption: Inverse-variance weighted mean of the per-run centroids and its statistical error.

an-isotope-shifts.name: birge-inflation
an-isotope-shifts.caption: Birge ratio and the extra scatter term added when runs disagree beyond their fit errors.

an-isotope-shifts.text: The Systematic Error group offers two modes:

items: Manual — one MHz value (spinbox, default 0) applied to every isotope.

Auto from cooler voltage & laser setpoint — estimate a per-project systematic from the run-to-run jitter of cooler voltage and laser setpoint, using the standard error of the mean. Set Charge (1–10) and Geometry (anti-collinear / collinear) for the Doppler sensitivity; projects with a single run get σ=0 (flagged unknown). A read-only details box reports each project's mean/std/SEM and combined systematic after Compute.

an-isotope-shifts.name: auto-sem
an-isotope-shifts.caption: Standard error of the mean used by Auto systematic estimation.

an-isotope-shifts.name: voltage-systematic
an-isotope-shifts.caption: Combined systematic from cooler-voltage SEM (via the Doppler sensitivity dν/dV) and laser-setpoint SEM.

an-isotope-shifts.text: Compute Shifts (green) runs the full pipeline and fills the Table tab — a 14-column report: Isotope, A, Centroid (MHz), σ_fit, σ_scatter, σ_corr, σ_volt, δν (MHz), σ_δν(stat), σ_δν(scatter), σ_δν(corr), σ_δν(sys), σ_δν, and Ref. If the [[an-reference-gp|GP correction]] is loaded and applied, its uncertainty (and inter-isotope covariance) is propagated into the δν columns.

an-isotope-shifts.name: isotope-shift
an-isotope-shifts.caption: Isotope shift relative to the reference and its statistical error (uncorrelated case).

items: Plot Options… opens a modeless window for layout (Stacked / Overlaid), content (Data + Model / Data Only), x-axis (Relative to Reference / Absolute), centroid lines, reference line, δν arrows (labelled in the compact value(err) MHz form), boxed per-isotope labels, sorting by A, colors, alpha, and z-order. Edit Plot (on the Plot tab) opens the [[plot-editor|Plot Editor]].
Send to Results writes the study (CSV + log + plot) to IS_<study>/iter_NNN and forwards it to the [[tab-results|Results]] tab.
Export Table CSV writes the shift table; Save Log writes the computation log.

an-isotope-shifts.caption: Isotope Shifts tab: the Isotope Entries table and Systematic Error group on the left, with the comparison plot (centroid lines and δν arrows) and the 14-column shift table on the right.

an-reference-gp.text: Inside the [[an-isotope-shifts|Isotope Shifts]] tab, the Reference Correction (GP) sub-tab trains a Gaussian process on time-stamped reference-isotope centroids to estimate and subtract slow wavemeter/laser-lock drift from your sample runs. The workflow is: fit a [[an-projects|Reference project]], fit the GP here, compute per-file corrections for sample projects, then re-fit those samples so the pipeline subtracts the drift.
Pick a Kernel, tick the reference projects to use, and click Fit GP (each fitted reference centroid becomes one training observation; at least two are required). The kernels are:

rows: Long campaigns with diurnal day/night lock cycles.

an-reference-gp.name: gp-rbf
an-reference-gp.caption: RBF kernel: smooth correlations decaying with time separation.

an-reference-gp.name: gp-matern
an-reference-gp.caption: Matérn 5/2 kernel: rougher sample paths than RBF.

an-reference-gp.name: gp-periodic
an-reference-gp.caption: Periodic factor used by the composite kernel to capture diurnal lock cycles.

an-reference-gp.text: Optionally tick Also run MCMC (with a draws spinbox, default 1000) for a diagnostic posterior; prediction and covariance still use the MAP point. After fitting, the diagnostic plot shows the reference scatter, the MAP curve, and 1σ/2σ bands.

an-reference-gp.name: gp-posterior
an-reference-gp.caption: GP posterior mean and variance at a query time; the training kernel adds per-observation and white-noise variance on the diagonal.

an-reference-gp.text: The GP needs PyMC. Without a C compiler on PATH, PyTensor falls back to a pure-Python path that is 10–100× slower; the panel shows a one-line hint telling you how to install a compiler. A fit typically takes 20–90 s.

Tick the sample projects under Apply to sample projects and click Compute per-file corrections. The table fills one row per successful run: Project, Run, t (h) (hours since the first run), Mode, μ (MHz), σ (MHz), and |μ|/σ. The Mode combo per row is Auto (use μ_GP), Manual (type your own μ and σ, e.g. a published value), or Off (skip that run). Rows are tinted amber above 2σ and red above 3σ of |μ|/σ; Off rows are greyed.

The Apply correction at fit time checkbox (default on) is a global gate: when off, the merge and fit pipelines ignore every per-file correction regardless of mode. The propagated correction uncertainty feeds the σ_corr columns of the shift table.

an-reference-gp.name: gp-propagated-sigma
an-reference-gp.caption: Correction-uncertainty contribution to an isotope shift, including the GP cross-covariance between sample and reference run times.

an-reference-gp.text: (Figure deferred — Reference Correction (GP) panel: kernel/MCMC/apply-toggle row, reference and sample project checklists, the diagnostic plot (scatter + MAP curve + 1/2σ bands), and the per-file corrections table.)

The trained GP, the table, and the per-row Mode choices all round-trip through the project YAML (see [[an-save-load]]). If corrections were saved but the GP itself was not, they are discarded on load and you are asked to re-fit.

an-running-fits.text: This page covers what happens after you click Run Fit on the [[an-fitter|Fitter block]]: how the fit runs, how to stop or revert it, and what lands on disk. Fits run off the GUI thread, so the window stays responsive and the block's progress bar and status line update live.

items: Separate mode fits each checked file independently across worker processes (up to your [[performance-settings|core limit]]), with a blended progress bar; a per-run timeout of 10 minutes (600 s) guards against a hung run.
Simultaneous mode runs one satlas2 Fitter over all files in a single worker.

Progress is mirrored to the global fit_progress signal so the [[status-bar|status bar]] reflects the active fit. On completion the status reports how many runs converged and, when applicable, to how many the [[an-reference-gp|GP correction]] was applied.

an-running-fits.text: ■ Stop cancels immediately and re-enables the UI; cancellation is cooperative — the fit aborts at the next optimizer iteration boundary — with a hard terminate kept only as a ~2 s backstop for a wedged simultaneous fit.

items: ↶ Revert restores the Model-block parameters to the snapshot taken just before the fit started (it does not delete output on disk).

Update iteration (on the [[an-output-block|Output block]]) regenerates artifacts for the last fit into its existing iter_NNN folder using the current output toggles, without re-running the fit — useful when you forgot to enable a plot or report.

an-running-fits.text: Results are written to a versioned iteration directory under <output_root>/analysis/<project>/iter_NNN/ and forwarded to the [[tab-results|Results]] tab. Depending on the Output-block toggles and whether the fit produced multiple runs, the iteration contains:

rows: Full block configuration used for this fit.
Text fit report (with correlations when enabled).
Per-run fitted parameter values and errors.
Per-run cooler V, laser setpoint, timestamps, applied centroid correction.
Per-run fit figures (.npz sidecars drive the live Results plots).
Parameter-vs-run / vs-time tracker plots (Separate mode, multi-run).
χ² maps and MCMC walk / correlation / confidence-band plots.
MCMC chain data when emcee was run.

an-running-fits.text: Trackers and the weighted-average CSV are only generated when a fit produced more than one run; a single-file fit skips them.
(Figure deferred — A Separate-mode fit in progress: the Fitter block's blended progress bar and status line, with Stop enabled and Run Fit disabled.)

an-save-load.text: The whole Analysis tab — every project plus the isotope-shift study — round-trips through one YAML file via the File menu's Save / Save As... (or Save Tab As... on this tab) and Load All... / Load Tab... (see [[save-load-config]]). The app save also records which iterations this session produced, so the Results tab restores exactly those on load.
The file stores everything under a top-level analysis key with two members:

an-save-load.code:
analysis:
  projects:        # one entry per project tab, block order preserved
    - project_name: ...
      ...
  isotope_shifts:  # the permanent Isotope Shifts study
    ...
an-save-load.caption: Top-level shape of an Analysis configuration YAML.

items: projects — each project's name, Sample/Reference kind, and its full block pipeline in order (Source, Model, Fitter, Output).

isotope_shifts — the [[an-isotope-shifts|Isotope Shifts]] entries, systematic settings, plot options, and the [[an-reference-gp|Reference Correction (GP)]] state (kernel, MCMC settings, the trained corrector, checked projects, and the per-file corrections table).

an-save-load.text: On load, projects are re-created in saved order and the isotope-shift study is restored. Source-block file paths are normalized cross-platform; if any referenced data file is missing, the shared relocate-or-skip flow runs, letting you locate or prune each missing file across all Source blocks. See [[missing-file-relocation]] for the details of that flow, which is the same one [[pa-save-load|Pre-Analysis]] uses.

Saving before fitting is fine. If the GP corrections were saved but the trained GP itself was not, the corrections table is dropped on load and you are prompted to re-fit the GP — this prevents the fit from silently using stale numbers.

res-layout.text: The Results tab is a two-pane browser for everything the [[tab-analysis|Analysis tab]] writes to disk. A horizontal splitter holds the project tree on the left and a stacked viewer on the right; clicking a tree item swaps the right pane to whatever fits that item.

The left pane is headed by a plain Analysis Results label above the [[res-tree|results tree]]. The right pane has a bold title label (initially Select an item to view) above a QStackedWidget, then a row of action buttons at the bottom. The splitter opens at roughly 280 px (left) / 700 px (right); drag the divider to rebalance.
The right-hand stack has five pages and shows exactly one at a time, chosen by the selected item's type:
See [[res-text-csv-image|viewing text, CSV and image items]] and [[res-live-plots|live plots]] for what each page does, and [[res-notes|notes]] for the editor.

Beneath the viewer sit Edit Plot, Export, Export All, a stretch, and an Info button (with a circle-help icon). Edit Plot is disabled until you select a plot or image; the others are always enabled. See [[res-plot-editor|the Plot Editor]], [[res-export|exporting]], and [[res-how-results-arrive|the Info button]].

res-layout.caption: The Results tab: the 'Analysis Results' tree on the left with a color-tinted project header and a highlighted NEW iteration, a live fit plot with its navigation toolbar on the right, and the Edit Plot / Export / Export All / Info button row at the bottom.

res-tree.text: The tree is a three-level hierarchy that mirrors the on-disk analysis output directory: Project → Iteration → output items. DENIS builds it by scanning each iteration folder, so items appear only when the corresponding file actually exists on disk.

Each Project row is bold and tinted with a stable hue derived from an md5 hash of the project name, so the same project always reads as the same color across sessions. Its Iteration rows share that hue at a dimmer shade. A freshly finished iteration (one that just completed this session and hasn't been opened yet) is shown bold in bright amber with a leading ● dot and a (NEW) marker; the highlight clears the first time you click anywhere inside that iteration. See [[res-how-results-arrive|how results arrive]].
For each iteration directory DENIS looks for and lists, in order:

items: Fit Report — fit_report.txt (text)
Parameters — parameters.csv (table)
Metadata — metadata.csv (table)
Binning Summary — binning_summary.csv (table)
Binning Warnings — binning_warnings.log (or legacy .json); the row is hidden when the warnings list was empty
Plots from the plots/, tracking/, and diagnostics/ subfolders
A Notes node (shown with a memo icon) at both project and iteration level

res-tree.text: Plot files prefer their .npz sidecar: when a .npz exists the item becomes a [[res-live-plots|live, re-renderable plot]] (shown with a .png name); standalone .png/.pdf/.svg files with no sidecar are listed as static images. Tracking CSVs are also surfaced. Figures named fit_run_<n> are sorted numerically (so fit_run_2 precedes fit_run_10), not lexically.

Internally each plot item carries a type tag — editable_plot (plots/tracking .npz), diagnostic_plot (diagnostics .npz), or image (static). All three open in the plot page; only the static images lack live data.

res-tree.caption: The results tree showing a hue-tinted project header, an iteration highlighted bold amber with the leading dot and (NEW) marker, and its expanded Fit Report / Parameters / Metadata / plot items beneath.

res-controls.text: Two button rows sit beneath the tree: a refresh/collapse row and a bulk-selection row. Together they let you re-sync the tree with disk and tick multiple projects or iterations for deletion.

rows: Re-scans the whole analysis output directory and surfaces results for every project found on disk, including projects not open in the Analysis tab.
Re-scans the output directory but loads only the project currently active in the [[tab-analysis|Analysis tab]] — faster when you have many on-disk projects.
Folds every project so the tree shows only top-level project names.

res-controls.text: Refresh only adds newly found projects and iterations; it never removes ones already in the tree. Use it to pick up runs done in another session or copied in by hand. Results from a fit you just ran are pushed automatically — see [[res-how-results-arrive|how results arrive]].

On Load All, the tree is seeded with exactly the iterations recorded in the save file (missing folders are reported in the status bar) — the whole-directory rescan only happens behind these Refresh buttons.

Every node carries a checkbox. Parents are tri-state: ticking a project cascades the tick down to all its iterations and items, and a parent recomputes to partially-checked when only some children are ticked. The second button row drives these:

items: Select All — ticks every project, iteration and item.
Unselect All — clears every tick.
Remove Selected — permanently deletes every ticked project / iteration (and its notes) from disk, after a single confirmation dialog that counts the projects and iterations involved.

res-controls.text: Remove Selected deletes directories from disk — it is not just a view filter. A ticked project subsumes its ticked iterations (only the top-most ticked node is deleted), and you confirm once for the whole batch. See [[res-delete|deleting projects and iterations]] for the per-row right-click alternative.

res-text-csv-image.text: Clicking a tree item first flushes any pending [[res-notes|notes]] and clears the iteration's [[res-tree|fresh highlight]], then routes the item to the matching viewer page based on its type.
Fit reports and binning-warning logs open in a read-only monospace box (Courier 10), read with errors="replace" so an odd byte never breaks the view. The Edit Plot button is disabled.

Parameters, metadata, binning-summary and tracker CSVs are loaded with pandas into a table whose columns auto-size to their content. Floating-point cells are formatted with %.6g; everything else is shown as plain text. If the file fails to parse, the error is shown in the text page instead. Edit Plot stays disabled for tables.

A standalone PNG/PDF/SVG with no .npz sidecar is drawn full-bleed into the plot canvas with its axes turned off and margins pushed to the figure edges, so it fills the pane like a picture rather than a chart. Edit Plot becomes enabled for images, but because there is no underlying data you can only restyle the rendered figure, not re-plot it.

Edit Plot is enabled for image and live-plot items and disabled for text, CSV and notes. For genuinely editable, re-renderable figures use the [[res-live-plots|live .npz plots]] instead of static images.

res-live-plots.text: This is the headline feature of the Results tab. When the Analysis tab saves a plot it writes the plot's data as a .npz sidecar next to the image. DENIS re-draws that data into a fully live matplotlib figure, so you get the navigation toolbar (pan, zoom, home/reset, save) instead of a flat picture — and you can [[res-plot-editor|edit it]].
Each .npz carries a plot_type key that selects the renderer. Eight types are supported:

rows: Time-of-flight histogram with the orange ToF-gate band
Stacked gated ToF (top) + gated spectrum (bottom), optional model overlay
The main fit plot (data, fit, components, residual)

res-live-plots.text: The fit renderer reproduces the saved PNG exactly: error bars clipped at y = 0 so the lower whisker never dips below zero, a smooth fit line, optional dashed per-component overlays (toggleable, initial visibility from the saved component_overlay flag), an optional 1σ band filled from MCMC samples, an optional residual panel sharing the x-axis at a 3:1 height ratio, and an optional hide-zero-bins mode that drops empty bins from the markers, residuals and component curves. Marker size and opacity auto-scale from the peak bin count so low-statistics runs render boldly. The area under the fit curve is shaded by default, and the on-plot fit-values box (when the fit was run with Fit values on plot) re-renders verbatim from the .npz. Tracker plots use unconnected points with a weighted-mean line and a horizontal ±1σ band, and all diagnostic axes carry unit-aware parameter labels.

res-live-plots.name: clipped-error-bars
res-live-plots.caption: The lower error bar is clipped at zero so count whiskers stay physical, matching the saved PNG.

res-live-plots.text: ToF panels build bin edges from the saved centers; see the bin-edge convention used across the live and saved plots:

res-live-plots.name: tof-bin-edges
res-live-plots.caption: Bin edges reconstructed from saved bin centers for the ToF stairs plot.

res-live-plots.text: Because tight_layout stores margins as size-dependent fractions, the layout is re-fitted on every canvas resize so the plot keeps hugging the border at any window size. After the data is drawn, any persisted [[res-style-json|.style.json]] overrides are applied on top.

(Figure deferred — A live fit plot rendered from a .npz sidecar: clipped error-bar data, the fit line, a residual panel below sharing the x-axis, and the matplotlib navigation toolbar above the canvas.)

res-plot-editor.text: Edit Plot opens the same Plot Editor used elsewhere in DENIS (see [[plot-editor|the Plot Editor dialog]]), wired to the live Results canvas. It is enabled only for plot and image items.

The dialog opens modeless (non-blocking) on purpose: mouse events still reach the canvas underneath, which is what makes click-to-select and drag-to-reposition work. All changes apply live to the canvas. The dialog has only a Close button — there is no separate Apply — and re-clicking Edit Plot while it is open simply raises the existing window rather than spawning a second one. Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y undo and redo edits inside the editor, and right-clicking the canvas offers the same Edit plot… entry.

rows: Per-axes title, x/y labels with font pickers and positions, sizes, limits, linear/log scale, ticks, grid
Every plotted artist with per-artist color, width, style, marker, alpha, visibility, position, rotation, z-order; font size/family/bold/italic for text; Remove artist
New text, annotations (text + arrow), lines, and spans — by coordinates or click-to-place
Legend visibility, location, font, frame, columns, title
Export DPI, Overwrite Original, Save as PNG / PDF / SVG

res-plot-editor.text: The Artists tab tags each entry by type so you can tell them apart: [EB] error bars, [L] lines, [S] scatter, [F] fills, [LC] line collections, [B] bars, [T] text, [A→] annotations, and [↔] standalone arrows. Tick Click to select / drag on plot to select an artist by clicking it on the canvas, and to drag text labels and annotation arrows to a new position.

When the dialog closes on a live .npz plot, DENIS captures the figure style and writes it to a sibling [[res-style-json|.style.json]] so the look persists across sessions. The Export tab's Overwrite Original and Save as … buttons feed into [[res-export|exporting]].

res-plot-editor.caption: The Plot Editor open modeless over a live fit plot, Artists tab showing [EB]/[L]/[S] entries and the 'Click to select / drag on plot' checkbox ticked.

res-style-json.text: Plot edits made in the Results tab survive sessions through a small JSON sidecar. When the [[res-plot-editor|Plot Editor]] closes on a live (.npz) plot, DENIS writes a .style.json file next to it; on the next render that style is re-applied automatically.
The path is derived from the .npz by stripping the last extension and appending .style.json — so fit_run_3.npz gets fit_run_3.style.json in the same folder.

res-style-json.code:
# fit_run_3.npz       <- saved plot data
# fit_run_3.style.json <- saved style overrides
# _style_path('.../fit_run_3.npz') == '.../fit_run_3.style.json'
res-style-json.caption: The style sidecar sits beside the .npz data file.

res-style-json.text: The style snapshot stores the figure size, suptitle and its size, subplot margins, and per-axes title / x&y labels (text, size, position) / limits / grid / tick size, plus every artist's style and the positions of text and annotation artists (including arrow tints).

On render, DENIS first draws the data from the .npz, then applies the style on top. Line/marker artists are matched positionally (by axes index and artist index, with a kind check that skips mismatches); text labels and the isotope-shift δν arrows are matched by their id tag (gid), so annotations always land on the right artist even when the renderer regenerates them. A removed_gids list records deleted tagged artists — they stay deleted across re-renders, and deletions accumulate across sessions.
Because matching is positional, hand-editing a .style.json or pairing it with a different .npz can map styles onto the wrong artists. Let the Plot Editor write it.
The Export tab's Overwrite Original button also rewrites the .style.json when it overwrites the image, keeping the sidecar in sync with the saved PNG. See [[res-export|exporting]].

Right-click a plot row for Copy plot style / Paste plot style. Both open a property checklist — figure size & margins, title & label text, font sizes, axis limits, grid, label positions, artist styles, text & annotations — so only the ticked groups travel. Paste preserves the target's own deletions, applies just the chosen properties (nothing else is reset), and a Paste style to N checked plots entry applies the clipboard in bulk.

res-export.text: Two buttons at the bottom of the right pane write results out: Export handles the single item you are viewing, and Export All copies an entire iteration directory.

items: For a plot or image, Export opens a Save Plot As dialog offering PNG, PDF or SVG; the figure is saved at 300 dpi with bbox_inches="tight". Any [[res-plot-editor|style edits]] you applied are baked into the output.
For a text or CSV item, Export is a plain file copy to a location you pick.

res-export.text: The export format is a per-dialog choice (the filter you pick in the Save As dialog), not a global setting. Save dialogs remember the last-used data directory.

Export All requires an iteration (select one, or any item inside it — a project header is refused with a hint), then copies that entire iteration directory verbatim to a destination folder you choose — reports, CSVs, plots, the .npz data and the .style.json sidecars all come along. It is a directory copy: it does not re-render plots, so the on-disk PNGs are copied exactly as they were saved.
Export All fails if the destination already contains a folder with the same iteration name — the copy uses copytree, which will not overwrite an existing directory.

Right-click any .npz-backed plot in the tree and choose Export data as CSV…. A dialog picks the columns (for a fit: x, y, y_err, the model curve, residuals and their errors, and the dense fit curve; other plot types export their own arrays), an optional header row, the delimiter (comma / tab / semicolon), and the decimal precision. Ragged columns are padded so the file always loads cleanly.
(Figure deferred — Export All copying an iteration directory: the destination picker open, and the resulting copied iter_xxx folder containing reports, CSVs, plots, .npz and .style.json files.)

res-notes.text: Every project and every iteration has a free-text Notes node (shown with a memo icon) where you can jot context, settings rationale, or to-dos. Notes are plain text and live inside the project / iteration directory.

Clicking a Notes node opens the notes editor page. Typing marks the note dirty and starts an autosave timer that fires roughly 800 ms after your last keystroke; the status label shows Editing… (autosaves) then Saved → <path>. A Save Now button forces an immediate write, and DENIS also flushes pending notes whenever you navigate to another item.
An empty, never-saved note isn't written to disk — DENIS only creates the file once there is actual text (or the file already exists).
Notes are deleted together with their owner. Deleting an iteration or project removes its notes file too, both via the right-click Delete and via Remove Selected. See [[res-delete|deleting]].

res-delete.text: There are two ways to permanently delete results from disk: a right-click menu on a single row, or the checkbox-based [[res-controls|Remove Selected]] for a batch. Both remove the directory itself, not just the tree entry.

Right-clicking a project or iteration row shows a contextual Delete… action (worded Delete iteration “…” or Delete project “…” (all iterations)). Leaf items like a single Fit Report or a plot deliberately get no delete entry, so you can't accidentally nuke one file out of an iteration. Choosing the action shows a Yes/No confirmation that names the directory before anything is removed.

items: The on-disk directory is removed first with shutil.rmtree.
The owner's [[res-notes|notes]] file is scrubbed explicitly, so a stray note never outlives its iteration or project.
Deleting a project removes all of its iterations.
The in-memory tree entry is dropped only after the disk delete succeeds.

res-delete.text: Deletion is permanent — there is no trash or undo. If the disk delete fails (for example, a file is locked), DENIS reports the error and keeps the in-memory tree entry so you can resolve the lock and retry.

res-how-results-arrive.text: Most of the time you never click anything to populate the Results tab — iterations show up on their own after a fit. This page explains the routes in, and the Info help button.

When an Analysis Run Fit finishes, the main window forwards the outputs to the Results tab (via add_results), which stores them and highlights the new iteration with the (NEW) [[res-tree|amber marker]]. DENIS does not switch you to the Results tab automatically — you may still be working in Analysis — so it flashes the status bar with a “click the Results tab to view” message and the average reduced chi-square. See [[an-running-fits|running and monitoring fits]].

The [[an-isotope-shifts|Isotope Shifts sub-tab]] has a Send to Results button that writes its comparison as an isotope_shift-type [[res-live-plots|live plot]] (plus a CSV) into an iteration directory, so the shift comparison lands in the same browser as the fits.
For results produced outside this session, or copied in by hand, use [[res-controls|Refresh All or Refresh Project]] to re-scan the output directory.
Loading a save file restores exactly the iterations the saved session produced — no whole-directory rescan. Folders that no longer exist are reported in the status bar.

The Info button (bottom-right, circle-help icon) opens a scrollable HTML help dialog summarising the tree structure, the viewer panels, Edit Plot, Export, and Refresh from Disk — a quick in-app reminder of what this tab does.

tool-schmidt.text: The Schmidt Moment Calculator predicts a nuclear magnetic moment from the single-particle shell model when no measured moment is available. It is a non-modal tool window (re-selecting it from the Tools menu just raises the existing window) and recalculates live on every change. The same backend feeds the Estimate tab, see [[est-schmidt-widget]].

Two radio buttons at the top pick the mode: Single particle (selected by default; for odd-mass nuclei with one unpaired nucleon) and Two particles (odd-odd nuclei, weak-coupling addition). Only the relevant input group is shown.

The orbital drop-downs list the standard jj-coupling shell-model orbitals from 1s1/2 through 1j15/2 (the same ordered table used throughout DENIS, up to the predicted magic 184). These are spherical shell-model states, not Nilsson orbitals.

The g_s quenching factor spinbox (range 0.01-2.0, default 1.000, 3 decimals) multiplies the free-nucleon spin g-factor before the moment is computed. Leave it at 1.0 for free-nucleon values; ~0.6-0.7 applies the commonly used effective (quenched) values. DENIS uses free-nucleon constants gs(p)=5.586, gs(n)=-3.826, gl(p)=1.0, gl(n)=0.0.

tool-schmidt.name: schmidt-proton
tool-schmidt.caption: Proton single-particle moment for the j = l + 1/2 (aligned) and j = l - 1/2 (anti-aligned) branches.

tool-schmidt.name: schmidt-neutron
tool-schmidt.caption: Neutron single-particle moment (orbital g-factor is zero, so only the spin term remains).

tool-schmidt.name: two-particle-lande
tool-schmidt.caption: Two-particle weak-coupling Lande addition rule; requires I > 0 (the Results show 'Set I > 0' otherwise).

tool-schmidt.text: The Results group shows three read-only fields: the moment μ (μn) in nuclear magnetons (6 decimals), the g-factor (single-particle g = μ/j; two-particle g = μ/I), and a one-line Description of the calculation including the g_s factor used.

tool-schmidt.name: g-factor
tool-schmidt.caption: g-factor from the single-particle moment and total angular momentum j.

Schmidt Moment Calculator in Two particles mode: Type 1/Orbital 1 and Type 2/Orbital 2 drop-downs, the Total I spinbox, the g_s quenching factor, and the live mu / g-factor / Description results for an odd-odd nucleus.

tool-shell-config.text: The Shell Configuration Plotter draws the nucleon shell-filling diagram for any nucleus and reports its proton/neutron configurations plus the predicted ground-state Jπ from the Nordheim coupling rule. It is a non-modal tool window. Enter Z and N on the left; the element symbol, mass A, and shell-model results update instantly, while the ladder diagram is drawn when you press Plot.

The Plot Options group controls the diagram. From shell: and To shell: pick the orbital range to draw (To shell defaults to 1g7/2, which covers most nuclei up to Z,N~50); if From is above To they are swapped automatically.

rows: Title with isotope label and Z, N
Draw hollow circles for empty slots
Only show vacancies on orbitals that have at least one nucleon
Prefix the principal quantum number in orbital labels
Circled magic-number labels in the gaps

tool-shell-config.text: Below the options, three read-only fields update live with Z/N: Proton config: and Neutron config: show the filled-orbital strings (closed core in brackets, valence orbitals outside), and Predicted Jπ: gives the Nordheim-rule ground-state spin-parity. For an odd-odd nucleus a coupled(...) annotation lists the two single-particle Jπ values being coupled.

tool-shell-config.name: nordheim-rule
tool-shell-config.caption: Nordheim coupling: J = |j_p - j_n| when the Nordheim number N is ~0, else j_p + j_n; parity from the product of the two orbital parities.

tool-shell-config.text: Press Plot to render the diagram in the scrollable right pane: protons are red on the left, neutrons blue on the right, with filled circles for occupied slots and hollow circles for vacancies, and magic numbers circled in the inter-shell gaps. After plotting, Edit Plot becomes enabled and opens the shared Plot Editor on the figure, see [[plot-editor]]. A matplotlib navigation toolbar sits above the canvas for pan/zoom/save.

tool-shell-config.caption: Shell Configuration Plotter for 72Ge (Z=32, N=40): left input/options panel with the live config strings and predicted Jpi, and the right-pane red-proton / blue-neutron shell ladder with circled magic-number gaps.

tool-shell-config.text: The orbital ladder uses standard spherical shell-model jj-coupling states; it is not a deformed (Nilsson) diagram.

tool-unit-converter.text: The Unit Converter expresses one laser-spectroscopy quantity in every other unit at once. It is a non-modal tool window; type a value and pick its unit, and all six output fields update immediately.

In the Input group, the Value: field is a scientific spinbox (accepts notation like 3.2e14, range 1e-15 to 1e15, default 532.0) followed by a unit drop-down. The Converted Values group lists one read-only field per supported unit; each value is shown to 6 significant figures, and the field matching the chosen input unit simply echoes your value.

Every input is first reduced to a wavelength in metres, then re-expanded to all six units. This routing keeps wavelength, frequency, and energy mutually consistent and uses CODATA values of h, c, and the eV conversion (see [[constants-units]]). A non-positive input produces zero in every output field.

tool-unit-converter.name: wavelength-conversions
tool-unit-converter.caption: The wavenumber / frequency / energy relations applied after reducing the input to a wavelength.
Unit Converter with 532 nm entered, showing the six read-only Converted Values fields (nm, cm^-1, MHz, GHz, THz, eV) filled simultaneously.

tool-shg.text: The SHG Crystal Angle Calculator computes the Type-I (o+o → e) phase-matching angle for second-harmonic generation in a nonlinear crystal, using Sellmeier dispersion. It is a non-modal tool window and recomputes live.
Only Type-I phase matching is implemented. There is no crystal Type selector and no refractive-index output; the dialog reports angle/wavelength and the SHG wavelength only.
The Crystal: drop-down offers BBO (190-3500 nm transparency), KDP (200-1500 nm), and LBO (160-2600 nm). The Mode: drop-down under Calculation Direction chooses what to solve for:

items: Wavelength → Angle — given the fundamental laser wavelength, find the crystal cut angle. The input is the Fundamental wavelength: spinbox (100-5000 nm, default 1064.00 nm).
Angle → Wavelength — given a cut angle, find which fundamental is phase-matched. The input is the Phase-matching angle: spinbox (0.1-89.9°, default 22.900°).

tool-shg.text: The dialog shows only the input relevant to the chosen mode, and in the Results group hides whichever field would merely echo the input. Results always include the SHG wavelength:, computed as the fundamental divided by two.

tool-shg.name: sellmeier
tool-shg.caption: Sellmeier dispersion used for the ordinary and extraordinary indices (lambda in micrometres). Coefficients are tabulated per crystal.

tool-shg.name: shg-phase-matching
tool-shg.caption: Type-I phase-matching condition n_e(theta, lambda_SHG) = n_o(lambda_fund), solved for sin^2(theta).

tool-shg.text: In Wavelength → Angle mode the angle is found in closed form; if sin²θ falls outside [0,1] the crystal cannot phase-match that line and the result reads No phase matching. In Angle → Wavelength mode DENIS samples the angle-vs-wavelength curve across the crystal's transparency range, brackets the requested angle, and bisects; if the angle is unreachable the result reads No solution.

tool-shg.caption: SHG Crystal Angle Calculator in Wavelength->Angle mode: BBO selected, 1064 nm fundamental, with the resulting phase-matching angle and 532 nm SHG wavelength.

tool-sfg-dfg.text: The SFG / DFG Calculator combines two input wavelengths into a sum-frequency (SFG) or difference-frequency (DFG) output and reports it in all six spectroscopic units. It is a non-modal tool window and recomputes live.

The Inputs group has two rows, Input 1: (default 1064 nm) and Input 2: (default 532 nm). Each is a high-precision scientific spinbox (preserving many significant figures, range 1e-15 to 1e15) paired with a unit drop-down, so either input may be given in nm, cm⁻¹, MHz, GHz, THz, or eV independently.
The Operation group has two radio buttons: Sum (SFG) (default) and Difference (DFG). SHG is simply the SFG special case where the two inputs are equal.

The calculator converts both inputs to wavenumber (which is additive in photon energy), combines them, and reports the generated wavelength in the Generated wavelength group with one read-only field per unit (6 significant figures). For DFG the magnitude of the difference is taken so the result is always positive; if the difference is zero the nm field shows ∞.

tool-sfg-dfg.name: sfg-dfg
tool-sfg-dfg.caption: Wavenumber-space combination: SFG adds the two wavenumbers, DFG takes the absolute difference.

tool-sfg-dfg.text: The combination is done in wavenumber space because adding or subtracting wavelengths directly is physically meaningless. To inspect a single value in all units instead of combining two, use the [[tool-unit-converter]].

tool-sfg-dfg.caption: SFG/DFG Calculator combining Input 1 = 1064 nm and Input 2 = 532 nm with Sum (SFG) selected, showing the six-unit Generated wavelength output.

tool-quick-plot.text: Quick Plot is a lightweight data viewer that lives outside the analysis pipeline, handy for sanity-checking a calibration file or any tabular data. It is a non-modal tool window with an embedded matplotlib canvas and toolbar.
The top of the window has two input tabs:

items: Load File — read a delimited file via Browse... (filter: *.csv *.tsv *.txt *.dat). The Delimiter: drop-down offers Auto, Comma (,), Tab (\t), Semicolon (;), and Space; Auto sniffs the first few lines. The first row is treated as column headers.

Enter Data — a built-in spreadsheet (starts 10 rows × 2 columns labelled X and Y). Buttons + Row, + Col, - Row, - Col, and Clear reshape it, and Paste from Clipboard imports tab/comma/semicolon/whitespace-separated data (auto-detecting whether the first row is a header).

tool-quick-plot.text: Below the tabs, pick the X: and Y: columns from drop-downs (Y defaults to the second column), the chart Type: (Line, Scatter, Step, or Bar), and a Color: via the colour swatch button (default crimson). Press Plot to draw; the plot also refreshes automatically when you change the X or Y column. Save writes the current data (headers + values) to a CSV or TSV file.

A settings row lets you set a Title:, an X label: and Y label: (both default to the column name if left blank), and toggle Grid (on by default) and Legend (on by default). The matplotlib toolbar above the canvas provides pan/zoom and its own image export.
Save and Browse dialogs reuse DENIS's remembered data directory, so they reopen where you last loaded or saved data, see [[data-directory-memory]].

tool-quick-plot.caption: Quick Plot with a CSV loaded on the Load File tab and a Line chart drawn: the X/Y column drop-downs, Type and Color controls, Title/label/grid/legend row, and the embedded canvas with toolbar.

opening-settings.text: DENIS keeps its application-wide preferences in one YAML file managed entirely through the Settings... dialog. Open it from File ▸ Settings... (see [[menu-bar]]). The dialog is a single scrollable window titled DENIS Settings, grouped into General, Performance, Output, Fitting Defaults and Plot Defaults, with OK and Cancel at the bottom.

Preferences are written to settings.yaml inside a settings/ folder next to the application (the project root), not in an OS config directory. The General group shows the exact path in a read-only field with an Open button (see [[general-settings]]). A missing or unreadable file simply returns empty defaults, so a fresh install or a corrupted file never blocks startup.

On first access DENIS migrates once from two older locations — ~/.cls_toolkit/settings.yaml and ~/denis/settings.yaml — by copying the first one found into the new path. This only happens when no new file exists yet.

items: OK writes every field to settings.yaml and immediately applies the plot rcParams (see [[plot-defaults-global]]). A theme change applies live; changing the UI scale or the verbose-log toggle additionally shows a Restart Required popup.
Cancel discards all edits made in the dialog; nothing is written.

opening-settings.text: These preferences are global to the app and are kept entirely separate from your project save files. Estimate/Pre-Analysis/Analysis state is saved with Save All / Save Tab to your own YAML (see [[save-yaml-format]]), never to settings.yaml.

opening-settings.caption: The DENIS Settings dialog scrolled to show the General, Performance, Output, Fitting Defaults and Plot Defaults group boxes, with OK/Cancel at the bottom.

general-settings.text: The General group holds the settings-file location and three behavior toggles that affect how DENIS reads paths and renders its UI.

rows: Shows the folder holding settings.yaml; Open reveals it in the OS file explorer.

When on (default), file paths in loaded save files are converted between Windows and POSIX conventions (drive-letter / slash and Nextcloud-mount heuristics) so a config made on another OS still resolves.
Dark (default) or Classic 98 (dark) — a retro look with Windows-98-style 3D bevels, sharp corners, navy selection, and a pixel font, in dark colors. Applies live on OK (settings key ui_theme).
Application scale factor, up to 3.0 in 0.25 steps. The special value Auto (stored as 0) lets Qt use the system DPI. Requires a restart.
A session log is always written under logs/ (newest 20 kept); this toggle raises the log level to DEBUG for extra diagnostic detail. Requires a restart.

general-settings.text: The UI scale is exported to the QT_SCALE_FACTOR environment variable, which must be set before the Qt application is created — hence the restart requirement. It is a true device-pixel scale, distinct from the font-only [[zoom]] in the View menu, which takes effect instantly. Try 1.25–1.50 on QHD screens and 1.75–2.0 on 4K.

general-settings.name: ui-scale-factor
general-settings.caption: The UI scale is written to QT_SCALE_FACTOR; a value of 0 (Auto) leaves it unset so Qt uses native system DPI.

general-settings.text: Changing either UI scale or Verbose session log raises a Restart Required dialog on OK, because both are read only at launch. All other settings apply immediately.

performance-settings.text: The Performance group has a single control: the maximum number of CPU cores the fitter is allowed to use in parallel.

rows: A read-only label showing the detected core count (os.cpu_count(), falling back to 4 if unknown).
Spinbox capped at the detected core count, ranging from 1 to that maximum. The default is the core count minus two (never below 1).

performance-settings.text: This cap applies to the parallel work in multi-source/simultaneous fits and to the multi-start [[an-autofitter|Auto-Fitter]]. Leaving two cores free by default keeps the rest of the system responsive while a long fit runs.
If the Auto-Fitter appears to hang or pin your machine, lower this value (or the number of starts) so fewer fits run at once.

output-settings.text: The Output group controls where DENIS writes run artifacts and how figures are saved to disk.

rows: The root output folder. Default ./output. Estimate runs land under <root>/estimates/ and Analysis runs under <root>/analysis/.
Auto (default) or Manual; governs how Analysis run iterations are numbered/created.
Default image format when figures are written to disk: png (default), pdf, or svg.

output-settings.text: The root directory is the single source of truth for output paths. Run ▸ Open Output Folder opens exactly this root, creating it first if needed (see [[run-open-output]]). Both subfolders are created on first write:

output-settings.code:
<output_directory>/
  estimates/   # Estimate-tab runs
  analysis/    # Analysis-tab project iterations & IS exports
output-settings.caption: Folder layout derived from the configured output root.

output-settings.text: Plot format and Plot DPI here are the on-disk save defaults. The interactive Figure/Save DPI used while a plot is on screen are separate values in [[plot-defaults-global|Plot Defaults]], and the Plot Editor's Export tab can override DPI per export.

fitting-defaults.text: The Fitting Defaults group seeds the values that new Analysis Fitter, Model, and Source blocks start with. These are starting points only — every block can be overridden in the [[tab-analysis|Analysis tab]].

rows: Checkbox, on by default — whether new fits report the parameter correlation matrix

fitting-defaults.text: Default method and Default statistics seed the [[an-fitter|Fitter block]]; the y-error model and x-column seed the [[an-source-block|Source block]]'s binning. The fit-statistic formulae and the y-error definitions are detailed in [[physics-fit-objectives]].
Changing a default here does not touch projects you have already built; it only affects blocks created afterward.

plot-defaults-global.text: The Plot Defaults group is a tabbed panel. Its first tab, Global, sets matplotlib rcParams applied to every figure DENIS draws. Each row seeds from your saved settings, or from the built-in _DEFAULT_PLOT_SETTINGS when unset.

The dialog exposes a single control for each of tick-label size, major/minor tick size, and tick width, but on save DENIS writes the value to both the xtick.* and ytick.* rcParams keys so the two axes always match.

Minor ticks are on by default app-wide (xtick/ytick.minor.visible), part of the bolder 2026-07 defaults. Existing settings files that had the old thin values materialized keep them — use Reset All Plot Defaults to adopt the new look.

After your settings (or defaults) are applied, DENIS layers a fixed _STATIC_PLOT_STYLE on top last: a serif/CMU font family, CM mathtext, ticks pointing inward, ticks on the top and right spines, and an opaque framed legend. Because it is applied after the user values, hand-editing the YAML cannot break the house style.

plot-defaults-global.code:
merged = dict(_DEFAULT_PLOT_SETTINGS)
merged.update(user_plot)          # your Global-tab values
plt.rcParams.update(merged)
plt.rcParams.update(_STATIC_PLOT_STYLE)   # applied last, immutable
plot-defaults-global.caption: apply_plot_settings() merge order (gui/shared_widgets.py).

plot-defaults-global.text: The Reset All Plot Defaults button at the bottom of the Plot Defaults panel restores both the Global tab and every per-type tab to the built-in defaults.

plot-defaults-per-type.text: Beside the Global tab, the Plot Defaults panel has one sub-tab per figure kind, each overriding the global style for just that kind of plot. The six tabs are Fit Plot, Walk Plot, Correlation, Chi-sq Map, Tracker, and Preview / TOF.

Each setting renders with the widget type inferred from its default value: booleans become checkboxes, floats and integers become spinboxes, and strings (such as matplotlib fmt strings or colors) become text fields. Hovering a row shows a per-key tooltip explaining what it does.

The Fit Plot tab is sectioned into Auto-sizing thresholds, Low-count region, Medium-count region, High-count region, a shared Base style, and Layout. When Auto-size by counts is on (default), the busiest bin's count selects a region, so low-statistics scans render with larger, more opaque markers and visible error-bar caps, while high-statistics scans get tiny transparent markers.

plot-defaults-per-type.name: autosize-by-counts
plot-defaults-per-type.caption: The busiest bin's count c selects the low/med/high region; its <region>_* keys override the base style.

plot-defaults-per-type.text: Turning Auto-size by counts off makes every fit use the unprefixed base-style values regardless of statistics.

A seventh block, isotope_shift_plot (boxed labels, shade-under-fit, arrow styling), has no sub-tab in this Settings dialog — edit it from the Output block's Plot Options… dialog, which exposes every per-type tab including Isotope Shifts and persists to the same settings keys. The fit plot's shade-under-fit and values-box options live there too.
Reset All Plot Defaults restores the Global tab and all per-type tabs at once.

plot-defaults-per-type.caption: The Plot Defaults → Fit Plot sub-tab showing the Auto-sizing thresholds group and the Low/Medium/High region groups with their per-region marker controls.

save-all-vs-tab.text: DENIS persists the three working tabs (Estimate, Pre-Analysis, Analysis) to YAML through five File-menu actions backed by dirty tracking. The Results tab has no YAML section and does not support Save/Load Tab.

rows: Writes to the currently loaded file with no dialog; falls through to Save As when none is loaded (or its folder is gone).
Always opens a dialog and writes estimate, preanalysis and analysis sections (plus the shared registries) to a chosen YAML.
Writes only the active tab's section, merging into an existing file so the other sections are preserved.
Populates whichever recognised sections are present in the file.
Loads only the active tab's section.

save-all-vs-tab.text: Save Tab As reads any existing file at the chosen path, replaces just the active tab's key, and rewrites the file — so saving the Analysis tab into a file that already holds an Estimate section keeps the Estimate intact. The shared registries (scan_filters, calibrations, calibration_acks, nist_asd) are refreshed on every save, and dropped from the file when empty.

Load Tab uses the same loader as Load All but only restores the active tab. If the requested section is absent it shows an information box listing the sections that are present. A legacy top-level Estimate file (keys at the root, no estimate: wrapper) is auto-detected when loading into the Estimate tab (see [[legacy-loading]]).

items: Save and Load remember separate last-used folders (last_config_save_dir / last_config_load_dir), each falling back to ./configs/ when the remembered path is gone (see [[data-directory-memory]]).
A .yaml extension is appended automatically if you omit it.
After Save, Save As, or Load All, the window title becomes DENIS v<version> - <filename>. Save Tab As / Load Tab report in the status bar but do not change the title.

save-all-vs-tab.caption: The File menu expanded showing Save All, Load All, Save Tab, Load Tab, Settings and Exit with their keyboard shortcuts.

save-yaml-format.text: A DENIS project YAML has up to three tab sections plus optional shared top-level blocks: scan_filters, calibrations (per-file voltage-calibration overrides), calibration_acks (acknowledged calibration warnings), and nist_asd (the NIST ASD Browser state). The file is written with keys in section order (not alphabetised).

save-yaml-format.code:
estimate:        # full estimation schema + a 'reference' sub-dict
  element: V
  Z: 23
  ...
preanalysis:     # {projects: [...]}
  projects:
    - files: [...]
      merged_entries: []
      plot_options: {...}
      ...
analysis:        # {projects: [...], isotope_shifts: {...}}
  projects: [...]
  isotope_shifts: {...}
scan_filters:    # optional, shared across tabs
save-yaml-format.caption: Top-level shape of a Save All YAML (see configs/V_analysis.yaml).

items: estimate mirrors the standalone [[estimation-yaml-schema|estimation schema]] (element, Z, transition, beam, laser, linewidth, scan, isotopes) plus a reference sub-dict carrying the reference isotope's A, I, μ, Q and the four A/B constants. and a last_run pointer to the latest estimation run folder.
preanalysis is multi-project: projects, each with a files list, merged_entries, plot_options, gate/binning, and models.
analysis = projects (the block pipelines) and isotope_shifts (the permanent IS sub-tab state).

save-yaml-format.text: Each entry in a Pre-Analysis or Analysis-Source files list carries its on-disk path plus its display state:

save-yaml-format.code:
- path: D:/05/14/run_7775.asdf
  color: '#000080'      # light-mode colour
  dark_color: '#00E5FF' # dark-mode colour
  alpha: 1.0
  linestyle: '-'
  checked: true
  centroid_offset_mhz: 0.0

save-yaml-format.text: The scan_filters block is shared across tabs, so a per-scan exclusion set in one tab is visible to the other on reload. Synthetic merged:// paths denote merged runs and are not real files. Ready-made examples ship in configs/.

estimation-yaml-schema.text: The Estimate tab's saved configs — and the standalone CLI estimator — use the schema validated by config_parser.load_config. The same content appears under the estimate: key of a full DENIS save.

items: element and Z
transition: lower_level_cm, upper_level_cm, J_lower, J_upper
beam: voltage_kV, charge_state, geometry
laser: harmonic plus exactly one of setpoint_cm or anchor
linewidth: fwhm_MHz
reference: A, I, mu, Q and the four A/B constants
scan: voltage_range_V (timing mode adds step_size_V, dwell_time_ms)
isotopes: a list of isotope blocks

estimation-yaml-schema.text: The parser rejects a laser block that specifies both setpoint_cm and anchor, and equally one that specifies neither (see [[est-laser]]). The anchor form names an isotope, a voltage offset dV, and an optional state (gs or isomer).

Timing is driven by a statistics block (required_sigma, optional uniform_timing). When the block is absent, the parser sets spectrum_only=True: no timing is computed and per-isotope rate/background fields are not required (see [[est-statistics]]).

In timing mode each isotope must specify either a flat background_rate_Hz or a TOF-gated background: {continuous_rate_Hz, tof_gate_us} block, which is converted to an effective rate using the dwell time.

estimation-yaml-schema.name: tof-gated-background
estimation-yaml-schema.caption: TOF-gated background folds the continuous rate by the gate-to-dwell duty cycle.

estimation-yaml-schema.text: An isomer sub-block (in timing mode) must give exactly one yield method: yield_ions_per_sec, production_ratio, or spin_distribution_sigma (see [[est-isomers]]). Optional top-level keys include g_s_factor (default 1.0) and uniform_timing; isotopes/isomers may carry a schmidt_valence sub-block.

estimation-yaml-schema.code:
element: Co
Z: 27
transition:
  lower_level_cm: 3350.494
  upper_level_cm: 47078.494
  J_lower: 5
  J_upper: 6
laser:
  setpoint_cm: 10920.071952
  harmonic: 4
beam: {voltage_kV: 29.9, charge_state: 1, geometry: anti-collinear}
linewidth: {fwhm_MHz: 100}
reference: {A: 59, I: 3.5, mu: 4.627, Q: 0.42,
  A_lower_MHz: 1056.8, B_lower_MHz: 0.0,
  A_upper_MHz: 333.52, B_upper_MHz: 0.0}
scan: {voltage_range_V: 100, step_size_V: 1.0, dwell_time_ms: 200}
statistics: {required_sigma: 3.0}
isotopes:
  - {A: 59, label: "59Co", I: 3.5, mu: 4.627, Q: 0.42,
     isotope_shift_MHz: 0.0, yield_ions_per_sec: 1.0e6,
     spectroscopic_efficiency: 0.001, background_rate_Hz: 10,
     peaks_to_measure: 3}
estimation-yaml-schema.caption: A minimal standalone Estimate config (configs/example_cobalt.yaml). Omitting the statistics block switches to spectrum-only mode.

legacy-loading.text: The loader is deliberately tolerant of older files so configs written by earlier DENIS versions (and the standalone estimator) still open cleanly.

items: Legacy top-level Estimate files. A file with element, Z, transition, or isotopes at the root (no estimate: wrapper) is auto-detected and routed to the Estimate tab on both Load All and Load Tab. configs/silicon_252_4.yaml is exactly this shape.
Optional keys default sensibly. Absent schema keys such as step_size_V, dwell_time_ms, or g_s_factor fall back to None or their documented default, so an older minimal file loads without error.
Legacy directory key. An old last_data_dir setting is still honoured as a fallback for the data-file picker (see [[data-directory-memory]]).
Pre-Phase save files. Newer per-file fields like centroid_offset_mhz and merge metadata are optional; files predating them round-trip unchanged.
Path conversion. When Auto-convert paths is enabled (default), file paths are converted to the current OS on load (see [[general-settings]]).
Binning stays faithful. A save written before the bin-definition key existed reloads with Auto binning (its original behaviour); only fresh tabs and new Source blocks default to Per scan step.

legacy-loading.text: Detection of a legacy Estimate file keys on the presence of element/Z/transition/isotopes at the top level. A modern multi-section file always wraps these under estimate:, so the two formats never collide.

missing-file-relocation.text: When a loaded YAML references data files that are no longer on disk, an interactive recovery flow runs before any tab is populated, so a moved folder or unmounted share never leaves the tabs half-built.

DENIS first scans the parsed YAML for every file path under preanalysis file lists and Analysis Source blocks, applies path conversion, and checks each for existence. Synthetic merged:// paths are skipped. If anything is missing, a Missing Files dialog lists the offenders (truncated to the first 8) and offers three choices:

rows: Opens a per-file picker for each missing entry, seeded from the previously located folder, then the original path's folder, then the YAML's folder. ASDF/VASDF paths get same-type filters. Cancelling a picker stops the loop; the rest stay missing and are pruned.
Prunes the broken references from the in-memory dict and loads everything else.

missing-file-relocation.text: When at least one path is successfully located, DENIS rewrites the updated paths back into the YAML on disk so the next load does not re-prompt (a status message confirms how many were updated). A Skip-only load leaves the file on disk unchanged, so you can retry the locate flow later — for example after remounting a network share.

missing-file-relocation.caption: The Missing Files dialog listing unresolved file paths with the Locate Files..., Skip Missing and Cancel buttons.

data-directory-memory.text: DENIS remembers separate last-used folders for different kinds of file dialogs, persisted in settings.yaml, so loading a config from one place never drags the data-file picker somewhere unexpected.

A remembered path that no longer exists is silently dropped: the config dialogs then fall back to ./configs/, and the data dialogs fall back to the current working directory. The data-load lookup additionally checks the legacy last_data_dir key, and writing a new data-load directory keeps that legacy key in sync, so users upgrading from an older version keep their picker context.
Plot save/export dialogs and the Quick Plot loader use the same data-directory helpers, so all data-side pickers share a coherent last-folder memory.

exit-prompt.text: Closing DENIS shows a confirmation dialog titled Close DENIS only when something actually changed since the last save or load (the app fingerprints the full save-state). An untouched or freshly-saved session closes silently; a dirty one offers Save (to the current file, or Save As when none is loaded), Don't Save, and Cancel.

rows: Writes to the current file (or opens Save As when none is loaded), then closes. Cancelling the Save As dialog keeps the application open.
Keeps the application open. This is the default button, so an accidental Enter or Esc is safe.

exit-prompt.text: Cancel is the safe default specifically to prevent accidental data loss. If you dismiss the dialog without choosing Save or Don't Save, the close is cancelled and nothing is saved.

split-file-editor.text: Edit ▸ Split File… opens a standalone, modal editor for turning one parent ASDF run into two virtual sub-runs. It needs no open project — it is purely a tool for producing .vasdf sidecar files that you can later load as independent runs in Pre-Analysis or Analysis (see [[pa-virtual-splits]]).

items: Click Open ASDF… to load a parent run; its raw scanning-voltage histogram is drawn. (Or Open existing .vasdf… to re-edit a split you made before — the parent ASDF loads automatically.)
Drag the cut marker on the plot, or type a value into Cut at raw voltage:, to set the split point.
Fill the two per-side metadata forms (the left side maps to suffix _A, the right to _B).
Click Save Split Files… to write one .vasdf per side next to the parent.

rows: Trailing token of the source name (Run_<id>) and of the .vasdf filename, e.g. 7509_A.
Optional free-form note, e.g. an isotope label.

split-file-editor.text: The parent ASDF is never modified — the editor only writes new .vasdf descriptor files alongside it. If clstools is not installed, the editor can still read existing .vasdf descriptors but cannot show the parent's spectrum.

split-file-editor.caption: The Split File editor: raw-voltage histogram with a draggable cut line and shaded left/right sides, the cut spinbox, and the two per-side metadata forms (Left → _A, Right → _B).

constants-units.text: This appendix collects every physics formula DENIS evaluates in its pure-NumPy / satlas2 backend (cls_estimations/). This first page fixes the physical constants and unit conventions used throughout; every later page builds on them.
All constants live in cls_estimations/constants.py and are SI-based. There is exactly one derived constant, CM_TO_HZ, used to turn wavenumbers (cm-1) into frequencies.

CM_TO_HZ = C_LIGHT * 100.0 = 2.99792458×1010 Hz/cm-1. Dividing by 106 gives the often-quoted MHz form, 29979.2458 MHz per cm-1 — DENIS hard-codes that value locally as CM1_TO_MHZ inside the systematic-error routine (isotope_shift.py).

items: Frequencies / detunings: MHz everywhere a line position, centroid, A/B constant, or isotope shift appears.
Laser setpoints and atomic energy levels: cm-1 (wavenumbers). The fundamental laser wavenumber is multiplied by the harmonic before any Doppler math.
Mass: atomic mass units (amu), converted to kg via AMU_TO_KG only inside the relativistic-β routine.
Acceleration / cooler voltage: volts (V). The Estimate beam field is entered in kV but stored as V.
Nuclear moments: magnetic moment μ in nuclear magnetons; spectroscopic quadrupole moment Q in barn.

constants-units.text: The rest-frame transition frequency is the wavenumber difference of the two levels converted to MHz (doppler.py, transition_frequency_MHz):

constants-units.name: transition-frequency
constants-units.caption: E_lower, E_upper in cm^-1; the factor c*100 is CM_TO_HZ, and /1e6 converts Hz to MHz.

physics-resonance.text: Two inversions of the relativistic Doppler relation let the Estimate tab place a known transition on the voltage axis. Both live in cls_estimations/doppler.py and share the geometry normaliser and the beam-energy β routines from [[physics-doppler]].

resonance_voltage(nu_rest, nu_laser, mass, charge, geometry) answers: at what acceleration voltage does a fixed lab-frame laser come into resonance with a known rest-frame line? It forms the ratio r = νlaser/νrest, solves the Doppler relation for β, then inverts β back to a voltage.

physics-resonance.name: resonance-beta
